rules.rule: The $800 duty-free de minimis entry is suspended for all non-postal shipments (courier, express, cargo) until CBP announces otherwise, so these parcels owe duty.
The $800 duty-free exemption for mail parcels is also suspended for goods arriving through the international postal network.

rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Bona fide gifts from a person abroad to a person in the U.S. may enter free up to $100 per recipient per day; purchases and bonus items do not count as gifts.

rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Mail shipments need a complete customs declaration and an invoice or value statement; shipments without them may be seized and forfeited.

rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Foreign-made articles, or their containers, must be legibly and permanently marked with the English name of the country of origin unless excepted.

rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Live birds and hatching eggs may enter only under APHIS rules; birds from regions with highly pathogenic avian influenza or Newcastle disease are generally barred.

rules.agency: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Dogs may enter only under CDC conditions, including a CDC import form and, from dog-rabies high-risk countries, a CDC dog import permit or approved arrival arrangements.

rules.statute: Fish and Wildlife Service regulations (50 CFR Part 14)
rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Importers of wildlife, including parts and products, must file Form 3-177 with the Fish and Wildlife Service where clearance is sought.

rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Importing any specimen of a CITES Appendix I, II or III species is unlawful unless CITES permit and document rules are met.

rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Plants for planting, including seeds, may be imported only after APHIS issues a written permit, unless the Plants for Planting Manual exempts them; apply at least 30 days ahead.

rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Imported plants for planting need a phytosanitary certificate naming at least the genus; small lots of seed may enter without one under specific permit conditions.

rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Imported fruits and vegetables must meet general entry conditions, such as being free of plant debris and unauthorized plant parts, plus any commodity-specific rules.

rules.statute: Prior notice of imported food (21 CFR Part 1, Subpart I)
rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Imported food needs FDA prior notice before arrival (2 to 8 hours by mode); for international mail it must be confirmed before mailing.

rules.statute: Prior notice of imported food (21 CFR Part 1, Subpart I)
rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Homemade food sent by an individual as a non-business personal gift to someone in the U.S. is exempt from prior notice.

rules.agency: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service
rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Meat products may be imported only from countries and establishments FSIS has found to have equivalent inspection systems.

rules.statute: Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act
rules.rule: FDA may refuse entry to cosmetics that appear adulterated or misbranded, were made under insanitary conditions, or are banned in their country of origin.

rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Cosmetics may not be made from or contain prohibited cattle materials, such as specified risk materials, unless an exemption applies.

rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Lithium cells and batteries carried into or within the U.S. must meet DOT hazmat rules; small cells get partial relief only within watt-hour and lithium-content limits.

rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Radio-frequency devices may be imported only if FCC-authorized, exempt and compliant, or covered by limited testing, trade-show or personal-use exceptions.

rules.agency: Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau
rules.rule: Businesses importing spirits, wine or beer into the U.S. must hold a basic importer permit from the Treasury (TTB).
Intoxicating liquors of any kind are nonmailable and may not be carried or delivered by the U.S. mail.
The Postal Service may not accept or deliver packages it believes contain cigarettes or smokeless tobacco; the narrow exceptions exclude international mail.

rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Imported cigars and cigarettes are released only in properly constructed packages bearing the quantity, kind and tax-class label required by tax regulations.

rules.agency: Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau
rules.rule: Tobacco products made in the U.S. and labeled for export may be brought back only to a manufacturer's export warehouse or in small personal-use quantities.

rules.statute: USPS Publication 52 — Hazardous, Restricted, and Perishable Mail
rules.rule: ENDS devices, parts, accessories and e-liquids are nonmailable, and the PACT Act exceptions do not extend to international mail.

rules.statute: Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act
rules.rule: New tobacco products, including e-cigarettes not on the U.S. market in 2007, need an FDA marketing order before they may be marketed.

rules.statute: Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDA personal importation policy)
rules.rule: Importing foreign drugs for personal use is generally illegal; FDA may use discretion for up to a three-month supply with a written personal-use statement and U.S. doctor details.

rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Importing Schedule I–II and narcotic controlled substances needs DEA registration and a per-shipment import permit; other scheduled substances need an import declaration.

rules.statute: Device registration and listing (21 CFR Part 807)
rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Foreign makers of devices offered for import must register with FDA, list their devices and name a U.S. agent.

rules.statute: Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDA personal importation policy)
rules.rule: Individuals generally may not import unapproved medical devices for personal use; fraudulent or counterfeit devices are refused.

rules.statute: Rough Diamonds Control Regulations (31 CFR Part 592)
rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Rough diamonds may be imported only if controlled through the Kimberley Process Certification Scheme.

rules.statute: Bank Secrecy Act regulations (31 CFR Chapter X)
rules.agency: FinCEN / U.S. Customs and Border Protection
rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Currency or monetary instruments over $10,000 mailed or shipped into the U.S. must be reported by the sender, or by the recipient if no report was filed.

rules.statute: Convention on Cultural Property Implementation Act regulations (19 CFR Part 12)
rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Cultural property stolen from a museum or monument of a State Party, and designated archaeological or ethnological material without the source country's export certificate, may not be imported.

rules.agency: Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives
rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Articles on the U.S. Munitions Import List, including firearms and many parts, need an ATF import permit, with limited exceptions such as minor parts under $100.

rules.statute: Switchblade Knife Act; Customs regulations (19 CFR Part 12)
rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Switchblade, butterfly, gravity and ballistic knives, including kits and parts, are not admissible; only non-automatic knives for utilitarian use enter unrestricted.

rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Imports bearing counterfeit versions of CBP-recorded trademarks are seized and forfeited unless the mark owner consents in writing.

rules.statute: CBP — Prohibited and Restricted Items (trademark and copyright)
rules.rule: Goods that infringe a registered trademark or a protected copyright may be detained or seized; handbags, accessories and clothing are the most common.
Duties and taxes are remitted on goods imported by mail with a value for duty of CAD 20 or less.
The CAD 20 mail remission does not apply to goods bought from a Canadian retailer, ordered through a Canadian address or phone, or imported by someone other than the buyer.
Courier imports from countries other than the U.S. and Mexico get duty and tax remission only up to a value for duty of CAD 20.
Courier imports from the U.S. or Mexico are duty-free up to CAD 150 and tax-free up to CAD 40 value for duty.
Goods under tariff items 9897.00.00, 9898.00.00 and 9899.00.00 (including prohibited weapons and obscene material) are prohibited imports.
Non-mailable international inbound items are removed from the mail at once and are not returned to the sender.
CBSA collects duty and tax on mail imports above the CAD 20 exemption and lists the amount on Form E14; Canada Post adds a handling fee.
Regulated animals (mammals, birds, turtles, tortoises, honeybees, hatching eggs) may be imported only under a CFIA permit or the import reference document conditions.

rules.statute: Wild Animal and Plant Protection and Regulation of International and Interprovincial Trade Act
rules.rule: Animals or plants, or their parts or derivatives, taken or traded in breach of a foreign state's law may not be imported.

rules.statute: Wild Animal and Plant Protection and Regulation of International and Interprovincial Trade Act
rules.rule: Regulated wild animals or plants, or their parts, may be imported only under a permit (CITES species).
Live animals are non-mailable unless accepted under a Canada Post agreement or listed in the Postal Guide, and parcels with animals banned by the Universal Postal Convention are refused.
Pests, or things that are or could be infested, including many plants and seeds, need a permit number and a foreign phytosanitary certificate unless CFIA has exempted them.
Regulated plant things must be declared to an inspector or customs officer at a designated place of entry when imported.
Importing a food whose sale is banned under section 4 of the Food and Drugs Act, such as poisonous, adulterated or unfit food, is prohibited.
Imported food must meet Canadian-equivalent safety controls, and the importer must give CFIA import information, including the licence number if licensed.
Food imported by an individual for non-commercial use within CFIA's maximum personal-use quantities is exempt from licensing.
An importer must notify Health Canada of each cosmetic within 10 days after first selling it in Canada.
Cosmetics that may injure users, contain filthy or foreign matter, or were made under unsanitary conditions may not be sold.
Dangerous goods are non-mailable unless offered under the Transportation of Dangerous Goods rules and Canada Post can carry them; UPU-banned dangerous items are refused.

rules.agency: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
rules.rule: Radio apparatus needing a technical acceptance certificate, or subject to technical standards, may not be imported or sold unless certified or compliant.

rules.agency: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
rules.rule: Jammers may not be imported, sold, possessed or used.
Intoxicating liquor may be imported into a province only if bought by or consigned to the provincial liquor authority, subject to listed exceptions.
Intoxicating beverages may enter Canada by mail only when sent to a licensed distiller or a provincially authorized body and at no more than 24% alcohol.
Tobacco products may not be sold, offered or possessed unless stamped as duty-paid, apart from listed licensee and transit exceptions.
Outside prescribed cases, only vaping licensees may sell, buy or possess vaping products that are not packaged and stamped as vaping-duty-paid.

rules.statute: Concentration of Nicotine in Vaping Products Regulations (SOR/2021-123)
rules.rule: Vaping products may not exceed 20 mg/mL nicotine, nor be sold in packages stating a higher concentration.

rules.statute: Health Canada guidance GUI-0116 (Bringing health products into Canada for personal use)
rules.rule: Canadian residents generally may not import prescription drugs by mail or courier; Health Canada may allow a 90-day supply or one course of treatment in some cases.
Substances in Schedules I to VI may not be imported into Canada except as the regulations authorize.
No one may import a food or drug for sale if selling it in Canada would breach the Food and Drugs Act or its regulations.
Class II, III and IV medical devices may not be imported or sold unless the manufacturer holds a Health Canada device licence.
Importers of medical devices need a medical device establishment licence, with exemptions for retailers, health care facilities and some manufacturers.

rules.statute: Export and Import of Rough Diamonds Act
rules.rule: Rough diamonds must arrive in a compliant container with a valid, accurate Kimberley Process Certificate from a participant.
Gold bullion, gold dust and non-manufactured precious metals are non-mailable unless under a Canada Post agreement.

rules.statute: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act; Cross-border Currency and Monetary Instruments Reporting Regulations
rules.rule: Importing currency or bearer monetary instruments worth CAD 10,000 or more, including by mail or courier, must be reported to the CBSA.

rules.statute: Cultural Property Export and Import Act
rules.rule: Foreign cultural property illegally exported from a reciprocating state may not be imported into Canada.
Importing firearms, prohibited or restricted weapons, devices, firearm parts or prohibited ammunition without authorization under the Firearms Act or other federal law is an offence.

rules.statute: CBSA Memorandum D19-13-2 (Customs Tariff item 9898.00.00; Criminal Code s. 84(1))
rules.rule: Prohibited weapons, including knives opening by gravity, centrifugal force or a button or spring, and other prescribed weapons, are prohibited imports.
Goods on the Import Control List, including many firearms and weapons, may be imported only under an import permit.
Goods, labels or packaging bearing an unauthorized mark identical or essentially identical to a registered trademark may not be imported, except personal-use goods in an individual's baggage.
Infringing copies made without the copyright owner's consent may not be imported, apart from personal-use copies in an individual's baggage.

rules.statute: Precious Metals Marking Act (R.S.C. 1985, c. P-19)
rules.agency: Department of Justice Canada (statute); Competition Bureau
rules.rule: A dealer who sells or imports into Canada a precious metal article bearing an unauthorized or improperly applied mark, or lacking a required mark, commits an offence.

rules.statute: Precious Metals Marking Act (R.S.C. 1985, c. P-19)
rules.agency: Department of Justice Canada (statute); Competition Bureau
rules.rule: Selling or importing a plated article marked to guarantee that its precious-metal plating will wear for any period is an offence.

rules.statute: Value Added Tax Act 1994 / Taxation (Cross-border Trade) Act 2018 (HMRC guidance)
rules.rule: Import VAT applies to all goods sent into Great Britain except gifts of £39 or less; for non-excise goods up to £135 the seller collects VAT at sale.

rules.statute: Customs duty on goods sent from abroad (HMRC guidance)
rules.rule: Customs duty is charged on goods over £135 and on excise goods of any value; duty is calculated on the price plus postage, packaging and insurance.
Parcels from outside the UK must be correctly declared by the sender; wrongly declared goods may be seized and the recipient fined or prosecuted.

Up to 5 pets may enter Great Britain under pet rules; selling, rehoming, more than 5 animals, exotic, wild or endangered animals trigger extra licence or certificate rules; invasive species are barred.

rules.statute: Animal and animal product import rules (Defra/APHA guidance)
rules.rule: Medium and high risk animals and animal products need a health certificate, importer declaration or import licence and entry via a border control post notified on IPAFFS.

rules.statute: CITES as applied in GB (Control of Trade in Endangered Species Regulations)
rules.rule: Importing CITES-listed animals, plants or derivatives needs a CITES permit; posted items need a CN22/CN23 plus the permit, and Border Force may seize items without one.

Plants and plant products from outside the EU, Switzerland and Liechtenstein need a phytosanitary certificate; for postal orders the seller must enclose it; over 2kg of plants for planting needs inspection.
Meat, meat products and milk-based products from outside the EU and listed nearby countries cannot be brought in for personal use, except limited infant or medical foods.
Because of animal disease outbreaks, personal imports from the EU of cheese, milk, dairy, pork, beef, lamb, goat, venison and their products are not allowed.

rules.statute: Cosmetic Products Enforcement Regulations 2013 / retained Regulation (EC) 1223/2009
rules.agency: Office for Product Safety and Standards
rules.rule: Every cosmetic product sold to GB consumers needs a Responsible Person with a UK address (not a PO box or mail forwarder) who ensures safety and notifies the product.

rules.statute: Duties and import VAT on gifts (HMRC guidance, international mail)
rules.rule: Perfumes with a flashpoint below 60°C are banned from international mail.
Posting any article likely to injure mail or postal staff is an offence unless the postal operator permits it; dangerous goods must follow the carrier rules.
Before placing radio equipment on the GB market, the importer must ensure conformity assessment, required marking and documentation are in place.

rules.statute: Excise duty on goods sent from abroad (HMRC guidance)
rules.rule: Alcohol sent from outside the UK is charged excise duty at current rates whatever its value and whether bought or a gift.

rules.statute: Duties and import VAT on gifts (HMRC guidance, international mail)
rules.rule: Undenatured ethyl alcohol and drinks above 24% ABV are prohibited in international mail; spirits over 35cl without a UK duty stamp may be seized.
Tobacco sent from abroad incurs excise duty at any value; cigarettes or hand-rolling tobacco lacking UK health warnings or fiscal marks can be seized.
Nicotine e-liquid for retail must be in refill containers of at most 10ml or single-use devices or tanks of at most 2ml; refillable tanks are capped at 2ml.
Pre-filled vapes and vaping liquids sent from abroad attract excise duty and may be seized if they lack Vaping Duty stamps.
Importing a controlled drug is prohibited except under an exemption or a Home Office licence and its conditions.
Importing medicinal products into Great Britain from outside approved countries requires a manufacturer licence; licensed imports also need wholesale and marketing authorisations.
Medical devices must be registered with MHRA before being placed on the GB market; manufacturers outside the UK must appoint a UK Responsible Person.
In trade, describing or supplying an unhallmarked article as gold, silver, platinum or palladium is an offence, subject to exemptions.
Importing ivory into the UK for sale or hire is prohibited dealing unless a statutory exemption applies.

rules.statute: Forgery and Counterfeiting Act 1981 (HMRC list of restricted goods)
rules.rule: Counterfeit protected coins and counterfeit currency notes are prohibited imports.
Cash of £10,000 or more carried into Great Britain from outside the UK must be declared; any cash suspected of criminal links can be seized.

rules.statute: Exporting or importing objects of cultural interest (DCMS guidance)
rules.rule: No licence is needed to import cultural objects into Great Britain, but goods leaving an EU state must comply with EU export licensing.
Importing or exporting illegally removed Iraqi cultural property is prohibited.
Importing the offensive weapons listed under section 141, such as flick knives, knuckledusters and similar bladed weapons, is prohibited.

rules.statute: Guns, knives, swords and other offensive weapons: UK border control (Home Office guidance)
rules.rule: Firearms and ammunition need a special licence to import; realistic imitation firearms and certain swords and knives are banned or only allowed in limited cases.

rules.statute: Trade Marks Act 1994 / Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988 (HMRC list)
rules.rule: Counterfeit, pirated and patent-infringing goods are prohibited imports where the right holder has lodged an application with HMRC; Border Force can seize them.
Since 1 July 2026 the duty exemption for e-commerce consignments up to €150 is abolished; a temporary €3 duty applies per item category until 1 July 2028.
Every non-EU parcel needs a customs declaration, usually by the carrier; import VAT of 19% or 7% applies, and Zoll expects a per-category handling fee from 1 November 2026.
Businesses self-declaring postal consignments up to €150 must use the IPK online declaration; oral declarations are no longer allowed, and IPK cannot be used for excise or restricted goods.
Private gifts up to €45, unpaid and non-commercial, are duty and VAT free; business senders or recipients and online purchases never qualify.

rules.statute: Produktsicherheitsrecht der EU, per Zoll guidance
rules.rule: Only products meeting EU product-safety rules may be imported; customs refers suspect parcels to market surveillance, which decides on release, return or destruction.

rules.statute: Tiergesundheitsrecht der EU (Heimtierverbringung), per Zoll guidance
rules.rule: Pet dogs, cats and ferrets need a microchip, valid rabies vaccination and official certificate; more than five animals fall under EU trade rules.
Pit bull terriers, American Staffordshire terriers, Staffordshire bull terriers, bull terriers and their crosses may not be imported into Germany.
Protected-species rules apply fully to postal imports, with no personal-use document exemptions as for travellers, except returned hunting trophies under conditions.
Plants, cut flowers, fruit and seeds from non-EU countries except Switzerland and Liechtenstein need a phytosanitary certificate; bananas, coconuts, dates, pineapples and durians are exempt.
Potatoes, even small quantities, are generally banned from postal import because of bacterial ring rot risk.

Meat, milk and products like cheese or sausage sent privately must meet commercial veterinary rules, border inspection and health certificates; fish up to 20kg and other listed goods up to 2kg are exempt.
Duty-free gift parcels may contain at most 50g of perfume or 0.25 litres of eau de toilette.
Fireworks are dangerous goods excluded from normal postal and courier shipping and are subject to special dangerous-goods transport rules.

rules.statute: Produktsicherheitsrecht der EU, per Zoll guidance
rules.rule: Importing signal jammers and laser pointers above one milliwatt is generally prohibited; other electrical and electronic devices must meet EU safety and conformity requirements.
Excise duty on alcoholic products is collected regardless of the parcel value.
Tobacco tax is paid by affixing German tax stamps; imported tobacco products and substitutes must bear a valid German tax stamp.
Nicotine e-cigarettes and refills may only be sold if refill containers hold at most 10ml, disposables or cartridges at most 2ml, and liquid nicotine is at most 20mg/ml.
E-liquids with or without nicotine and disposable e-cigarettes are taxed as tobacco substitutes and need a German tax stamp on import, regardless of parcel value.
Medicines requiring German authorisation may only be brought in if authorised here; non-EU imports need a recipient holding an import licence.
Private individuals may generally not receive medicines by post or courier from abroad; only a German pharmacy may order unavailable medicines on prescription.
Importing narcotics without a licence from the Federal Institute for Drugs and Medical Devices is not permitted.
Rough diamonds sent from a non-EU country into Germany must have a valid Kimberley certificate.
If unaccompanied cash of €10,000 or more enters Germany by post or courier, customs may require a disclosure from sender or recipient within 30 days.
Importing cultural property is banned if it left another state in breach of its national-treasure law, EU restrictions or the Hague Protocol.
Cultural goods in Part A of the annex may not enter the EU if illegally exported from a non-EU country; some categories need an import licence or importer statement.
Import of Iraqi cultural property and objects of archaeological, historical or religious importance removed illegally is prohibited.
Handling weapons or ammunition listed as prohibited in Annex 2 Section 1 of the Weapons Act is banned.
Bringing weapons or ammunition into Germany from a non-EU country needs a prior permit from the German weapons authority, also for postal shipments.
EU customs enforce intellectual property rights at the border under Regulation 608/2013, allowing suspected counterfeit goods to be detained.
Counterfeit goods in post are checked by customs; buying even one fake item from an online shop counts as commercial and can lead to seizure.

rules.statute: Zoll guidance on private food imports (Tschernobyl-Strahlenschutzmaßnahmen)
rules.rule: Wild mushrooms and wild berries from certain non-EU countries need prior border-post testing and a CHED-D document, except up to 2 kg dried or 10 kg fresh for own use.

rules.statute: EU protective measures for food of non-animal origin, per Zoll guidance
rules.rule: Some foods of non-animal origin face EU or national protective measures requiring certificates and official checks. Private non-commercial parcels of e.g. tea, spices or sesame may be exempt up to 5 kg fresh or 2 kg other.
Food supplements or vitamin products, especially those presented as treating disease, can count as medicines in Germany and then fall under medicines law, regardless of the selling country's rules.
Sturgeon caviar needs CITES documents when imported by post; unlike travellers, postal imports get no exemption even for small personal quantities.

rules.statute: Gesetz über den Feingehalt der Gold- und Silberwaren (FeinGehG)
rules.rule: Gold and silver goods may be made and sold in any fineness, but a fineness mark may only be applied as the Act allows; jewellery fineness must be stated in thousandths, error limit 10/1000.

rules.statute: Gesetz über den Feingehalt der Gold- und Silberwaren (FeinGehG)
rules.rule: No fineness may be stated on gold or silver goods filled with other metals or metallically joined to reinforcements of other metals.

An importer may place radio equipment on the market only after the manufacturer's conformity assessment, with CE marking and required information, and if it can operate in at least one EU state without breaching spectrum rules.

A dealer may make radio equipment available only after checking the CE marking, required information and importer details; suspected non-conforming equipment must be held back and risks reported to the Bundesnetzagentur.

rules.agency: European Union regulation (directly applicable in DE)
rules.rule: A medical device whose manufacturer is outside the EU may be placed on the EU market only if the manufacturer designates a sole EU authorised representative, accepted in writing.

rules.agency: European Union regulation (directly applicable in DE)
rules.rule: Importers may place only conforming devices on the market; they must first check CE marking, EU declaration of conformity, an authorised representative, labelling and instructions, and UDI, and add their own name and address.

rules.agency: European Union regulation (directly applicable in DE)
rules.rule: A cosmetic may be placed on the EU market only if an EU-established responsible person is designated; for imported cosmetics each importer is the responsible person unless it mandates another EU person in writing.

rules.agency: European Union regulation (directly applicable in DE)
rules.rule: Before a cosmetic is placed on the market, the responsible person must notify the Commission electronically of its category, name, responsible person, country of origin for imports, target Member State and contact details.

rules.statute: Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 concerning batteries and waste batteries
rules.agency: European Union regulation (directly applicable in DE)
rules.rule: Importers may place a battery on the market only after verifying its EU declaration of conformity, technical documentation, CE marking and labelling, and instructions and safety information in a language end-users understand.

rules.statute: Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 concerning batteries and waste batteries
rules.agency: European Union regulation (directly applicable in DE)
rules.rule: Producers, including distance sellers supplying end users directly, may make batteries, also those inside appliances, available in a Member State only if they or their EPR authorised representative are registered in that Member State's producer register.

Goods worth AUD 1,000 or less generally pay no duty or tax at the border (overseas sellers may collect GST at sale); above AUD 1,000 an Import Declaration and duties apply. Tobacco and alcohol are excluded.
Low-value goods arriving by air or sea cargo need a free self-assessed clearance declaration; goods arriving by post do not.
Goods named in the prohibited imports regulations need written permission; importing without it can lead to seizure and penalties up to 2,500 penalty units or 10 years' prison.

rules.agency: Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry
rules.rule: All international mail is screened for biosecurity risk; goods must be accurately described on the postal declaration, and non-compliant items are treated, re-exported or destroyed at the importer's cost.

rules.agency: Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry
rules.rule: Cats and dogs enter only under strict conditions; bird hatching eggs need a permit; personal imports of reptile and amphibian eggs are not allowed.

rules.statute: Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999
rules.agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
rules.rule: CITES-listed animals and products need the origin country's export permit and a DCCEEW import permit; live specimens must also be on the permitted live import list.
Domestic cat and dog fur and goods containing it need prior permission before import.

rules.agency: Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry
rules.rule: Seeds must be a BICON-permitted species, carry a phytosanitary certificate, and arrive commercially packed with the full botanical name; khapra beetle host seeds are banned.

rules.agency: Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry
rules.rule: Most live plants cannot be imported without a DAFF import permit and post-entry quarantine.

rules.agency: Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry
rules.rule: Food sent by mail is checked against BICON conditions; meat has strict, fast-changing rules, and canned meat is accepted only from approved foot-and-mouth-free countries.

rules.agency: Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry
rules.rule: Whole eggs for eating cannot be imported without an import permit.
Cosmetics containing more than 250 mg/kg of lead need written permission to import; lead-acetate hair treatments are excepted.

rules.agency: Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry
rules.rule: Commercially made and packaged cosmetics for personal use are allowed up to 10 kg or 10 L; other cosmetics may need a biosecurity permit.
Disposable, novelty or refillable cigarette lighters with a customs value of AUD 5 or less cannot be imported.
Mobile phone, GPS, wi-fi and drone jammers are banned: they cannot be imported, possessed, supplied or used.
Radio devices sold online, by post or in person must meet ACMA standards; small online sellers face the same rules and penalties as large retailers.
Alcoholic drinks are outside the AUD 1,000 low-value rule; duty and taxes are payable whatever the value.

Cigarettes, loose and shisha tobacco and heat-not-burn sticks need import permission obtained in advance, and all duty is due at the border; cigars and up to 1.5 kg of oral tobacco are exempt from the permission rule.

Vaping devices, accessories, substances and liquid nicotine cannot be imported without permission, which goes only to licensed commercial importers or researchers; individuals cannot import vapes, even with a prescription.

Personal Importation Scheme: own or immediate-family use only, never for resale; an Australian prescription is needed for prescription-only medicines, at most a 3-month supply (15 months per year), in original packaging.
Drugs listed in Schedule 4 of the import regulations, with their isomers and derivatives, need an import permit.

rules.article: Personal Importation Scheme conditions (TGA; no section cited on page)
rules.rule: Counterfeit medicines are banned from import in all cases, even with a prescription; known fakes are seized.
Importing a medical device that is not on the Australian Register of Therapeutic Goods is an offence unless an exemption, such as personal importation, applies.

rules.article: Personal Importation Scheme conditions (TGA; no section cited on page)
rules.rule: Counterfeit medical devices cannot be imported under any circumstances.
Rough diamonds can only be imported in a tamper-resistant container with a Kimberley Process certificate from a participating country.

rules.statute: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2006
rules.rule: Moving monetary instruments worth AUD 10,000 or more into Australia, including by mail or courier, must be reported; commercial carriers carrying for others are excused.

rules.statute: Protection of Movable Cultural Heritage Act 1986
rules.rule: Foreign protected cultural objects that were illegally exported from their home country may be seized and returned; Australia issues no permission to import them.
Firearms, parts, magazines, ammunition and imitation firearms need import permission and, in many cases, police certification.
Daggers, butterfly, push, ballistic, automatic, concealed and throwing knives need Home Affairs permission or police certification before import.
Importing and selling counterfeit goods is illegal and can be prosecuted; Customs may seize goods that infringe a trade mark under a notice of objection.
Importing counterfeit credit, debit or charge cards is prohibited without written permission.

rules.statute: Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956, per ABF list of prohibited goods
rules.rule: ABF's prohibited-goods list names cheap lighters (AUD 5 or less) as the only consumer battery/hazmat item; no national import ban on lithium batteries found. Carrier dangerous-goods rules apply.

rules.statute_en: Customs Tariff Act (JP)
rules.agency: Japan Customs (MOF Customs and Tariff Bureau)
rules.rule: Imports with a total taxable value of JPY 10,000 or less per postal package are free of customs duty and consumption tax, except leather bags, knitwear and leather shoes; liquor and tobacco taxes remain due. Split shipments are added together.

rules.statute_en: Customs Act (JP)
rules.agency: Japan Customs (MOF Customs and Tariff Bureau)
rules.rule: Mail valued at JPY 200,000 or less clears through simplified postal customs and is delivered with any tax notice; above JPY 200,000 the addressee must file an import declaration and pay taxes before release.

rules.statute_en: Customs Act (JP)
rules.agency: Japan Customs (MOF Customs and Tariff Bureau)
rules.rule: Goods requiring a permit, approval or inspection under other laws must prove it to customs before import is allowed, including food, plant, animal, pharmaceutical, wildlife, weapon and chemical controls.

rules.statute_en: Customs Act (JP)
rules.article: 第69条の11第1項第7号・第8号
rules.agency: Japan Customs (MOF Customs and Tariff Bureau)
rules.rule: Books, images, carvings and other articles harmful to public security or morals, and child pornography, may not be imported.

rules.statute_en: Act on Domestic Animal Infectious Diseases Control (JP)
rules.rule: Designated animals (cloven-hoofed animals, horses, poultry, rabbits, honeybees) and their products need an exporting-government health certificate and inspection by animal quarantine, whether sent by cargo or mail.

rules.statute_en: Act on Domestic Animal Infectious Diseases Control (JP)
rules.rule: Animals, carcasses and animal products from regions designated by MAFF (for example disease-affected areas) may not be imported without a ministerial research permit.

rules.statute_en: Rabies Prevention Act (JP)
rules.rule: Dogs, cats, raccoons, foxes and skunks may only be imported after animal quarantine.

rules.statute: 外国為替及び外国貿易法
rules.statute_en: Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Act (JP)
rules.rule: CITES-listed animals and plants, including skins, leather goods, carvings and traditional medicines, need the exporting country's CITES permit and, where required, a METI import approval; only certain customs offices clear them.

rules.statute_en: Plant Protection Act (JP)
rules.rule: Plants and plant parts, including seeds and fruit, need a phytosanitary certificate from the exporting government and plant quarantine inspection, whatever the quantity or purpose and including international mail. Highly processed items such as dried fruit or tea are exempt.

rules.statute_en: Plant Protection Act (JP)
rules.rule: Soil, plants with soil attached, quarantine pests, and specified plants from designated regions may not be imported unless MAFF permits it for research. Soil is banned from every country, including soil packed in novelty goods.

rules.statute_en: Food Sanitation Act (JP)
rules.rule: Food, additives, utensils, packaging and infant toys imported for sale or business use need a food import notification at a quarantine station each time; personal-use imports are exempt.

rules.statute_en: Act on Domestic Animal Infectious Diseases Control (JP)
rules.rule: Meat products such as sausage, ham and jerky need an exporting-government certificate even as gifts or by mail; parcels without one are refused, and illegal mailed imports have led to arrests.

rules.statute: 主要食糧の需給及び価格の安定に関する法律
rules.statute_en: Act on Stabilization of Supply, Demand and Prices of Staple Food (JP)
rules.rule: Rice for personal use is limited to 100 kg per person per year across baggage, mail and courier, and must be notified before clearance; other rice imports require an import levy.

rules.statute: 医薬品、医療機器等の品質、有効性及び安全性の確保等に関する法律
rules.statute_en: Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Act (JP)
rules.rule: Cosmetics may be imported as a business only by a licensed marketing authorisation holder; individuals may import up to 24 standard-size units per item for own use without an import confirmation.

rules.statute_en: Electrical Appliances and Materials Safety Act (JP)
rules.rule: Businesses importing regulated electrical products must notify METI within 30 days of starting and may sell them only with the PSE mark.

rules.statute_en: Customs Act (JP)
rules.article: 第69条の11第1項第3号・第4号
rules.agency: Japan Customs (MOF Customs and Tariff Bureau)
rules.rule: Explosives and gunpowder-type goods, including fireworks, may not be imported except by persons authorised under other laws.

rules.statute_en: Customs Act (JP)
rules.agency: Japan Customs (MOF Customs and Tariff Bureau)
rules.rule: High-pressure gases, poisons and deleterious substances, pesticides and other regulated chemicals need approval under their own laws before customs will clear them.

rules.statute_en: Radio Act (JP)
rules.agency: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications
rules.rule: Operating a radio station needs a licence from the Minister of Internal Affairs unless it is a very weak station or certified low-power equipment; imported wireless devices without conformity marking may be unlawful to use.

rules.statute_en: Food Sanitation Act (JP)
rules.agency: Japan Customs (MOF Customs and Tariff Bureau)
rules.rule: Liquor up to 10 kg for personal use needs no food notification; imports for sale need a food import notification and a liquor sales licence. Liquor tax is due even under the JPY 10,000 duty exemption.

rules.statute_en: Tobacco Business Act (JP)
rules.agency: Japan Customs (MOF Customs and Tariff Bureau)
rules.rule: Importing cigarettes, cigars or other tobacco for sale needs registration as a specified retailer with the Finance Minister; personal imports need none. Tobacco taxes are due even when the parcel is under JPY 10,000.

rules.statute: 医薬品、医療機器等の品質、有効性及び安全性の確保等に関する法律
rules.statute_en: Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Act (JP)
rules.rule: Without an import confirmation, individuals may import only own-use medicines: prescription, poisonous or powerful drugs up to one month's dose, other medicines up to two months, topicals up to 24 units per item. Commercial import needs a licence.

rules.statute_en: Customs Act (JP)
rules.agency: Japan Customs (MOF Customs and Tariff Bureau)
rules.rule: Narcotics, psychotropics, cannabis, opium and poppy straw, stimulants and opium pipes may not be imported, except by the government or licensed persons.

rules.statute_en: Customs Act (JP)
rules.agency: Japan Customs (MOF Customs and Tariff Bureau)
rules.rule: Designated substances under the pharmaceutical law may not be imported except for approved medical uses; some herbs, aroma oils and bath salts sold as legal contain them.

rules.statute: 医薬品、医療機器等の品質、有効性及び安全性の確保等に関する法律
rules.statute_en: Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Act (JP)
rules.rule: Individuals may import only home-use devices, one set each, and up to two months of disposable contact lenses, without confirmation; professional devices cannot be imported by individuals and commercial imports need a licence.

rules.statute_en: Foreign Exchange Order (JP)
rules.rule: The advance report for precious metals above the set weight applies when they are carried in person; mailed precious metals are outside this reporting duty.

rules.statute_en: Customs Act (JP)
rules.agency: Japan Customs (MOF Customs and Tariff Bureau)
rules.rule: Counterfeit, altered or imitation coins, banknotes, revenue or postage stamps and securities, and illegally made or blank payment cards, may not be imported.

rules.statute_en: Foreign Exchange Order (JP)
rules.rule: The advance report for cash or securities above JPY 1 million applies to amounts carried in person; other import modes are exempt from it under this order.

rules.statute: 文化財の不法な輸出入等の規制等に関する法律
rules.statute_en: Act on Controls on the Illicit Export and Import of Cultural Property (JP)
rules.rule: Specified foreign cultural property, stolen from a designated institution abroad, can only be imported with an import approval under the Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Act.

rules.statute_en: Customs Act (JP)
rules.agency: Japan Customs (MOF Customs and Tariff Bureau)
rules.rule: Pistols, rifles, machine guns, cannons, their ammunition and pistol parts may not be imported except by persons authorised under other laws.

rules.statute: 銃砲刀剣類所持等取締法
rules.statute_en: Firearms and Swords Control Act (JP)
rules.agency: National Police Agency / Prefectural Public Safety Commission
rules.rule: Guns, crossbows, swords with blades of 15 cm or more and daggers or switchblades of 5.5 cm or more need a possession permit or registration certificate, plus METI import approval, before customs clears them.

rules.statute_en: Customs Act (JP)
rules.agency: Japan Customs (MOF Customs and Tariff Bureau)
rules.rule: Goods infringing patents, utility models, designs, trademarks, copyright, neighbouring rights, circuit layouts or plant breeder rights may not be imported.

rules.statute_en: Customs Act (JP)
rules.agency: Japan Customs (MOF Customs and Tariff Bureau)
rules.rule: Trademark- or design-infringing goods mailed by an overseas business to a private individual in Japan are prohibited, even if the buyer intends only personal use.

rules.statute: 医薬品医療機器等法 (PMD Act), per 近畿厚生局 guidance (Q&A Q67)
rules.agency: 近畿厚生局 (MHLW Kinki Regional Bureau)
rules.rule: Nicotine e-cigarettes are medicines in Japan. Customs-only clearance is capped at 1,200 cigarettes or 12,000 puffs, 60 cartridges or 120 ml liquid; more needs an import confirmation backed by a doctor's prescription.

rules.statute: 医薬品医療機器等法 (PMD Act), per 近畿厚生局 guidance
rules.agency: 近畿厚生局 (MHLW Kinki Regional Bureau)
rules.rule: Personal imports of medicines, including nicotine e-liquids, are for the importer's own use only; selling or giving them to others is prohibited by law.
Goods arriving by post or air with a CIF value of S$400 or less get import GST relief, except liquor and tobacco; above S$400, GST is charged. Sea and land imports get no relief.
Since January 2023, GST-registered overseas vendors charge GST at checkout on low-value goods (sale price S$400 or less per item) sent by air or post, so it is not charged again at import.

rules.statute: Regulation of Imports and Exports Act 1995
rules.rule: Controlled goods need authorisation from the competent authority before import; postal and courier imports also need a customs permit when the authority requires it, whatever the value.
For postal parcels the addressee is the importer; SingPost collects any GST or duty through its app, kiosks or post offices before delivery, and couriers collect it from the buyer.

rules.statute: Regulation of Imports and Exports Act 1995
rules.rule: Obscene articles, publications and videos, and seditious or treasonable materials, cannot be imported into Singapore.
No animal, bird or veterinary biologic may be imported or transhipped without a licence from the Director-General.

rules.statute: Regulation of Imports and Exports Act 1995
rules.rule: Rhinoceros horn and its parts or powder, and endangered wildlife species and products derived from them, cannot be imported into Singapore.
CITES-listed animals and plants and their parts need CITES permits before entering Singapore, including ivory bought abroad; violations carry fines up to S$50,000 per specimen.

rules.statute: SingPost General Prohibition & Dangerous Goods (carrier rule, IATA DG classes)
rules.rule: SingPost will not bring live animals into Singapore, for example bees, leeches or silkworms.

rules.statute: SingPost General Prohibition & Dangerous Goods (carrier rule, IATA DG classes)
rules.rule: SingPost will not bring live plants into Singapore, for example orchids or roses.

rules.agency: Director-General under the Control of Plants Act
rules.rule: Importing or transhipping fresh fruits or vegetables requires both a licence and a permit.

rules.statute: Regulation of Imports and Exports Act 1995
rules.rule: Food imported for sale needs an SFA licence or registration and an import permit for every consignment; receiving and selling food or samples by parcel post still counts as commercial import.

rules.statute: SingPost General Prohibition & Dangerous Goods (carrier rule, IATA DG classes)
rules.rule: SingPost will not bring perishable food, such as meat, fish, vegetables or fruit, into Singapore.

rules.statute: Regulation of Imports and Exports Act 1995
rules.rule: Chewing gum cannot be imported, except oral dental and medicinal gum approved by the Health Sciences Authority.
Cosmetics supplied in Singapore must meet the Health Products Act and ASEAN Cosmetic Directive regulations, and a product notification is usually needed before sale.

rules.statute: SingPost General Prohibition & Dangerous Goods (carrier rule, IATA DG classes)
rules.rule: SingPost will not carry dangerous goods into Singapore: explosives, gas and aerosols, flammable liquids and solids, oxidisers, toxic substances, radioactive material, corrosives such as lead-acid batteries, magnetised items, dry ice.

rules.statute: SingPost General Prohibition & Dangerous Goods (carrier rule, IATA DG classes)
rules.rule: Lithium batteries are accepted only installed in equipment, undamaged, at most 4 cells or 2 batteries per package, within 20 Wh per cell or 100 Wh per battery (lithium-metal 1 g or 2 g).

rules.statute: Regulation of Imports and Exports Act 1995
rules.rule: Scanning receivers, military communication gear, telephone voice changers, jammers, and radio equipment on 880-915, 925-960, 1900-1980 or 2110-2170 MHz (except cellphones or IMDA-approved equipment) cannot be imported.
Liquor is dutiable: customs and excise duty plus GST apply at any value, and the S$400 GST relief for post and air never covers it.
Tobacco is dutiable at any value. Tobacco arriving by parcel post must follow standardised packaging rules or be returned, and importing for sale needs an HSA tobacco licence.
Chewing tobacco, shisha, smokeless cigarettes, dissolvable nicotine, snuff, gutkha, khaini, zarda and topical or injectable nicotine products cannot be imported, sold or possessed.
E-cigarettes, vaporisers, their components and nicotine liquids cannot be imported, even with no nicotine or for quitting smoking; the ban covers free trade zone re-exports.

Personal medication up to a three-month supply may be brought in with a valid prescription and original labelled packaging; controlled substances need prior HSA approval, and only immediate family may be supplied.

Controlled drugs in the Fourth Schedule to the Misuse of Drugs Regulations, including cannabis products, cannot be imported; nicotine medicines bought abroad and gene-therapy products are also barred from personal import.

Personal import of medical devices needs prior HSA approval, at most three months' supply. Radiation-emitting or practitioner-administered devices are not allowed, and repeat shipments suggesting resale are rejected.
Importing, wholesaling or manufacturing medical devices as a business requires an HSA dealer's licence.
Investment precious metals meeting IRAS criteria are GST-exempt; by air no permit is needed at CIF S$400 or below, above that a GST relief permit is required. Ordinary jewellery is taxed normally.

rules.statute: Corruption, Drug Trafficking and Other Serious Crimes (Confiscation of Benefits) Act 1992
rules.agency: Singapore Police Force (Suspicious Transaction Reporting Office)
rules.rule: Physical currency and bearer negotiable instruments moved into Singapore, and cash received from outside Singapore, must be reported under Part 6A.

rules.statute: SingPost General Prohibition & Dangerous Goods (carrier rule, IATA DG classes)
rules.rule: SingPost will not bring coins, banknotes or other valuables into Singapore.

rules.statute: SingPost General Prohibition & Dangerous Goods (carrier rule, IATA DG classes)
rules.rule: Ammunition, fireworks, flares and caps for toy firearms will not be carried by SingPost into Singapore.
Customs can seize imports suspected of infringing a registered trade mark, copyright, geographical indication or registered design, on a rights holder's notice or on its own initiative.

Plants and seeds sent by parcel need a phytosanitary certificate from the exporting country and an NParks import permit (S$11 per consignment) applied for at least 2 working days before arrival; CITES species also need a CITES permit.

Seeds for sowing (except economic crops) and bare-rooted plants need no additional declarations; plants with growing medium need a nematode-free declaration or nematicide treatment endorsed on the certificate.

rules.statute: Guns, Explosives and Weapons Control Act 2021 (replaced the Arms and Explosives Act)
rules.agency: Licensing Officer under the Guns, Explosives and Weapons Control Act 2021
rules.rule: Importing a weapon listed in the First Schedule, such as crossbows, bows, arrows, swords, machetes or bayonets, is an offence unless the importer holds an import licence, a class licence or a statutory exemption.

rules.statute: Guns, Explosives and Weapons Control Act 2021 (replaced the Arms and Explosives Act)
rules.agency: Licensing Officer under the Guns, Explosives and Weapons Control Act 2021
rules.rule: Importing a gun, a major part of a gun or a gun accessory is an offence unless the importer holds an import licence, a class licence or a statutory exemption.
Hong Kong charges duty only on liquor, tobacco, certain hydrocarbon oils and methyl alcohol; other imported goods pay no customs duty.
Importers must lodge an import declaration within 14 days; postal packets whose contents are worth under HK$4,000 are exempt.
Schedule 1 articles (pesticides, medicines, Chinese medicines, rough diamonds, frozen or chilled meat and poultry, scheduled chemicals) need an import licence.
Strategic commodities, including high-performance computers, advanced chips and munitions, need a TID import licence per shipment.
Anything whose import or circulation is forbidden in Hong Kong may not be sent by post.

rules.article: reg. 11; Public Health (Animals and Birds) Ordinance (Cap. 139)
rules.rule: Mammals, birds and reptiles may only be imported with an AFCD permit obtained in advance.

rules.statute: Protection of Endangered Species of Animals and Plants Ordinance (Cap. 586)
rules.rule: Appendix I species need an AFCD import licence; Appendix II and III imports need the exporting country's CITES permit and inspection on landing, plus a licence for live wild Appendix II animals.
Animal carcasses and products from dogs or cats, such as dog skin, need an AFCD permit before import.
Plants need an AFCD Plant Import Licence and the origin country's phytosanitary certificate; seeds need only the phytosanitary certificate unless they are scheduled species.
Plants grown in and imported from mainland China are exempt from the plant import licence, as are cut flowers, fruit and vegetables for eating.
Importing plant pests or soil is banned unless AFCD has authorised it in advance.

rules.statute: Imported Game, Meat, Poultry and Eggs Regulations (Cap. 132AK)
rules.rule: Game, meat, poultry and eggs need a health certificate from a recognised issuing entity at origin and, for game or eggs, prior FEHD permission.
Frozen or chilled meat and poultry need an FEHD import licence per consignment; only up to 15 kg in personal baggage is exempt.

rules.statute: Public Health and Municipal Services Ordinance (Cap. 132)
rules.rule: Milk and milk drinks, frozen confections and foods with colourings, sweeteners, preservatives or metals face specific import or composition rules.

rules.statute: Reserved Commodities (Control of Imports, Exports and Reserve Stocks) Regulations (Cap. 296A)
rules.rule: Rice import licences go only to registered stockholders; up to 15 kg in personal luggage is exempt.
Importing regulated mercury-added products is banned, including cosmetics with mercury content above 1 ppm.

rules.article: Sch. 1 Munitions List; Dangerous Goods Ordinance (Cap. 295)
rules.rule: Explosives on the Munitions List need a TID import licence with prior endorsement, plus Dangerous Goods Ordinance controls.
Waste batteries are hazardous waste; importing them needs an EPD permit.
Radio transmitting apparatus can only be imported under an OFCA permit unless the importer holds a Radio Dealers Licence (Unrestricted).
Liquor above 30% alcohol by volume is dutiable; importing it needs a Customs licence, and duty is paid before release.
Wine and other liquor of 30% alcohol by volume or less carry a 0% duty rate.
Tobacco imports need a Customs licence and attract duty, for example HK$3,306 per 1,000 cigarettes.
Importing smokeless tobacco products is banned.
Importing alternative smoking products, including e-cigarettes, heated tobacco, herbal cigarettes and their parts and liquids, is an offence; only transit and air transhipment cargo are exempt.
Medicines need a Department of Health import licence; buying medicines online and having them sent from overseas without a licence breaches Cap. 60.
Dangerous drugs need a Department of Health import licence and import certificate, plus the exporting country's authorisation.
Proprietary Chinese medicines and 36 listed Chinese herbal medicines need a Department of Health import licence.
Rough diamonds can only be imported by TID-registered traders with a Kimberley Process import certificate.

rules.statute: Cross-boundary Movement of Physical Currency and Bearer Negotiable Instruments Ordinance (Cap. 629)
rules.rule: Importing currency or bearer instruments worth over HK$120,000 as cargo in one batch needs an advance electronic declaration; mail packets are excluded from this cargo rule.
Arms, including air guns over 2 joules, stun guns, pepper sprays and crossbows over 6 kg, need Police licences; Munitions List items also need a TID import licence.
Prohibited weapons such as knuckledusters, gravity knives, throwing darts and spring-loaded batons cannot lawfully be possessed.
Importing goods bearing a forged trade mark or a false trade description is an offence; goods in transit are excluded.

rules.statute: 郵包物品進出口通關辦法
rules.statute_en: Regulations Governing Customs Clearance of Postal Parcels (TW)
rules.rule: Postal or express e-commerce imports with dutiable value up to NT$2,000 are exempt from duty, commodity tax and VAT; above that the full value is taxed. Tobacco, alcohol and tariff-quota farm goods never get the exemption.

rules.statute: 郵包物品進出口通關辦法
rules.statute_en: Regulations Governing Customs Clearance of Postal Parcels (TW)
rules.agency: MOF Customs Administration (郵包物品進出口通關辦法, via MOJ law DB)
rules.rule: The duty-free rule stops applying from the 7th exempted shipment per recipient in a half-year (Jan-Jun, Jul-Dec). Postal parcels from the same sender arriving the same day to the same recipient are valued together.

rules.statute: 郵包物品進出口通關辦法
rules.statute_en: Regulations Governing Customs Clearance of Postal Parcels (TW)
rules.article: 第3條第3款、第6條第1項第1款（快遞70公斤：not stated on the official page）
rules.agency: MOF Customs Administration (郵包物品進出口通關辦法, via MOJ law DB)
rules.rule: A postal parcel may weigh at most 30 kg; an express (courier) consignment at most 70 kg. Postal items over USD 5,000 FOB need a formal customs declaration.

rules.statute: 郵包物品進出口通關辦法
rules.statute_en: Regulations Governing Customs Clearance of Postal Parcels (TW)
rules.rule: Express goods subject to any import regulation (food, supplements, drugs, animal/plant products, pet food, medical devices) cannot use the simplified e-commerce declaration; a formal import declaration and agency approval are needed.

rules.statute_en: Customs Act (TW)
rules.rule: Controlled goods, contraband, IP-infringing goods, live animals/plants and protected wildlife products do not qualify as express consignments.

rules.statute_en: Statute for Prevention and Control of Infectious Animal Diseases (TW)
rules.agency: MOA Animal and Plant Health Inspection Agency (APHIA)
rules.rule: Quarantinable animals and animal products may not be sent by post; posted items are returned, confiscated or destroyed, and failing to surrender them is fined NT$30,000-150,000.

rules.statute_en: Plant Protection and Quarantine Act (TW)
rules.rule: Plants, seeds and bulbs are in principle barred from post since 2019-06-20, unless APHIA lists the item as certificate-exempt or the recipient gets a mail-import permit first and an export phytosanitary certificate is attached.

rules.statute_en: Plant Protection and Quarantine Act (TW)
rules.rule: Soil, plants with soil attached, live insects and other pests may not be brought in; importing pests or soil-bearing plants is a criminal offence (up to 3 years).

rules.statute_en: Statute for Prevention and Control of Infectious Animal Diseases (TW)
rules.article: 第28條第1項第2款、第43條第8款
rules.agency: MOA Animal and Plant Health Inspection Agency (APHIA)
rules.rule: Pork products may not be posted from countries with African swine fever; the recipient is fined NT$200,000 the first time and NT$1,000,000 from the second time.

rules.statute_en: Statute for Prevention and Control of Infectious Animal Diseases (TW)
rules.rule: Meat products and other quarantinable animal products (including processed meats such as cured pork, bones, chicken feet) may not be sent by post; importing banned animal products risks up to 7 years and NT$3m fine.

rules.statute_en: Act Governing Food Safety and Sanitation (TW)
rules.rule: Personal-use food may skip TFDA import inspection only within limits; it must not be resold.

rules.statute_en: Act Governing Food Safety and Sanitation (TW)
rules.rule: Since 2015-12-01 personal tablet/capsule foods sent by post or freight may be released by customs without TFDA inspection within the 12-per-product / 36-total limit (original packs).

rules.statute: 郵包物品進出口通關辦法
rules.statute_en: Regulations Governing Customs Clearance of Postal Parcels (TW)
rules.agency: MOF Customs Administration (郵包物品進出口通關辦法, via MOJ law DB)
rules.rule: Pet food up to 6 kg by post needs no feed-import registration certificate; other import rules (e.g. quarantine) still apply.

rules.statute: 化粧品衛生安全管理法
rules.statute_en: Cosmetic Hygiene and Safety Act (TW)
rules.rule: Personal-use cosmetics may be imported but not sold, given away for trial or passed on; violation fined NT$10,000-1,000,000. The former 12/36 personal quantity limit for special-purpose cosmetics was repealed 2024-07-01.

rules.statute: 化粧品衛生安全管理法
rules.statute_en: Cosmetic Hygiene and Safety Act (TW)
rules.rule: Cosmetics packed in glass ampoules need TFDA approval before import, including when posted or sent by express.

rules.statute_en: Commodity Inspection Act (TW)
rules.rule: Goods with secondary lithium batteries in BSMI-listed categories need commodity inspection; without it they cannot enter (fine NT$200k-2m), may be ordered returned.

rules.statute_en: Regulations Governing Exemption from Commodity Inspection (TW)
rules.agency: 商品免驗辦法 (BSMI, via MOJ law DB)
rules.rule: Non-sale personal items in BSMI-inspected categories are exempt and released directly by post when within value/quantity limits; IT equipment has a 5-item limit.

rules.statute: 郵包物品進出口通關辦法
rules.statute_en: Regulations Governing Customs Clearance of Postal Parcels (TW)
rules.article: 第7條第2項、第14條第2項第1款
rules.agency: MOF Customs Administration (郵包物品進出口通關辦法, via MOJ law DB)
rules.rule: Posted alcohol is always taxed (no NT$2,000 exemption). Up to 5 litres for personal use needs no tobacco-and-alcohol importer licence.

rules.statute: 郵包物品進出口通關辦法
rules.statute_en: Regulations Governing Customs Clearance of Postal Parcels (TW)
rules.article: 第7條第2項、第14條第2項第2款
rules.agency: MOF Customs Administration (郵包物品進出口通關辦法, via MOJ law DB)
rules.rule: Posted tobacco is always taxed. Personal use within limits needs no importer licence.

rules.statute_en: Tobacco Hazards Prevention Act (TW)
rules.article: 第15條第1項第2款、第26條第2項
rules.rule: E-cigarettes and all other imitation tobacco products and their parts are banned from import since 2023-03-22; non-business importers face NT$50,000-5,000,000 fines.

rules.statute_en: Tobacco Hazards Prevention Act (TW)
rules.article: 第7條第1項、第15條第1項第3款
rules.rule: Heated tobacco without an approved MOHW health-risk assessment may not be imported; customs check postal and express parcels. Page (2023) says none was approved yet.

rules.statute_en: Pharmaceutical Affairs Act (TW)
rules.rule: Sending ordinary medicines to Taiwan by post requires prior TFDA approval (personal-use drug import).

rules.statute_en: Controlled Drugs Act (TW)
rules.rule: Controlled drugs may not be sent by post or express.

rules.statute_en: Medical Devices Act (TW)
rules.rule: Listed personal medical devices may be posted under easy clearance once per half-year within limits; others need a TFDA import permit; resale fined up to NT$1m.

rules.statute_en: Wildlife Conservation Act (TW)
rules.rule: Endangered-species products (e.g. listed in CITES) need CITES permits; protected wildlife products are excluded from express channels.

rules.statute: 槍砲彈藥刀械管制條例
rules.statute_en: Controlling Guns, Ammunition and Knives Act (TW)
rules.agency: 槍砲彈藥刀械管制條例 (MOJ law DB)
rules.rule: Guns, ammunition and listed knives may not be made, sold or transported without central authority permission; unlicensed transport of knives carries up to 3 years.

rules.statute_en: Customs Act (TW)

rules.statute_en: Regulations Governing Trade between the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area
rules.rule: Mainland foods not opened for import (e.g. mushrooms, peanuts, vermicelli, rice) may not be posted; small-quantity exemptions do not apply.

rules.statute: 臺灣地區與大陸地區貿易許可辦法
rules.statute_en: Regulations Governing Trade between the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area
rules.rule: Of mainland teas only Pu'er is open for import; green, black, oolong and other mainland teas may not be imported.

rules.statute: 臺灣地區與大陸地區貿易許可辦法

rules.rule: Controlled mainland goods (e.g. noodle products, printed bed textiles) need a trade permit plus the competent agency's consent (TFDA, BSMI).

rules.statute: 臺灣地區與大陸地區貿易許可辦法
rules.statute_en: Regulations Governing Trade between the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area
rules.rule: Mainland alcohol not opened for import is capped at 1 litre for travellers; no postal-specific figure was found.

rules.statute: 臺灣地區與大陸地區貿易許可辦法
rules.statute_en: Regulations Governing Trade between the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area
rules.rule: Mainland antiques, religious relics and artworks are an allowed import category, but they need a Trade Administration permit unless exempted.

rules.statute_en: Cultural Heritage Preservation Act (TW)
rules.rule: Century-old cultural objects brought in temporarily for exhibition or repair and later taken out need prior application.

rules.statute_en: Money Laundering Control Act (TW)
rules.rule: Cash, securities and gold above set thresholds must be declared, including when sent by courier or post; undeclared foreign currency above the limit is confiscated.

rules.statute: 洗錢防制物品出入境申報及通報辦法
rules.statute_en: Regulations on Declaring and Reporting Goods Crossing the Border under the Money Laundering Control Act (TW)
rules.rule: Declaration thresholds: foreign/HK/Macao cash over USD 10,000, NT$ over NT$100,000, securities over USD 10,000, gold over USD 20,000; post counted per recipient per arrival day.

rules.statute: 臺灣地區與大陸地區人民關係條例
rules.statute_en: Act Governing Relations between the People of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area
rules.rule: Mainland-issued currency may not enter Taiwan above the FSC limit; travellers seal the excess with customs. Numeric limit not stated on the official pagein fetched text.

rules.statute_en: Customs Act (TW)
rules.rule: Counterfeit or altered currency and securities, and plates for printing fake money, may not be imported.

rules.statute: 洗錢防制物品出入境申報及通報辦法
rules.statute_en: Regulations on Declaring and Reporting Goods Crossing the Border under the Money Laundering Control Act (TW)
rules.rule: Gold worth over USD 20,000 arriving by post for one recipient on one arrival day must be declared.

rules.statute: 郵包物品進出口通關辦法
rules.statute_en: Regulations Governing Customs Clearance of Postal Parcels (TW)
rules.rule: Ordinary jewellery follows the general postal duty rules (NT$2,000 duty-free threshold).

rules.statute: 大陸地區發行之幣券進出入臺灣地區限額規定（依臺灣地區與大陸地區人民關係條例第38條訂定）
rules.statute_en: Limits on Mainland-Issued Currency Entering or Leaving Taiwan (under Cross-Strait Act Art. 38)

rules.statute: 中央銀行公告（新臺幣現鈔進出境；經財政部關務署出入境常見問題轉述）

rules.statute: 空運快遞貨物通關辦法
rules.statute_en: Regulations Governing Customs Clearance of Air Express Consignments (TW)
rules.rule: Air express consignments must weigh 70 kg or less per piece and must not be banned, controlled, IP-infringing, fresh farm produce, live plants/animals or protected wildlife; otherwise they cannot clear in the express zone.

rules.statute: 海運快遞貨物通關辦法
rules.statute_en: Regulations Governing Customs Clearance of Sea Express Consignments (TW)

rules.statute_en: Regulations for the Carriage of Dangerous Goods by Ships (TW)

rules.rule: Sea dangerous-goods channel only: ships on international routes must handle, document and stow dangerous goods per the IMDG Code; dangerous goods fall into nine classes (Annex 1). UN3480/3481/3090/3091 are not named here; they are in the incorporated IMDG list (not stated on the official pageon official pages).

rules.statute_en: Regulations for the Carriage of Dangerous Goods by Ships (TW)
rules.agency: MOTC Maritime and Port Bureau (MOJ law database)
rules.rule: Sea dangerous-goods channel only: the shipper must give the shipowner, carrier or master a signed dangerous-goods consignment note and correctly classify, pack, mark and label the goods.

rules.statute_en: Ship Act (TW)
rules.rule: Sea dangerous-goods channel only: ships carrying dangerous goods need a classification-society carriage document noted on their inspection certificate; the loading rules above are issued under this article.

rules.statute: 中华人民共和国海关法
rules.statute_en: Customs Law of the PRC
rules.agency: NPC Standing Committee (text via MFA PDF)
rules.rule: Personal items received by post must be for own use and in reasonable quantity.

rules.agency: Customs Tariff Commission of the State Council / MOF
rules.rule: Personal parcels up to RMB 2,000 (or one indivisible item) are taxed at simplified rates; tax of RMB 50 or less is waived; excess quantities are taxed as goods.

rules.rule: Fresh fruit and vegetables, cut flowers, tobacco leaf, seeds, seedlings and other propagating material, and soil may not be posted in.

rules.statute: 中华人民共和国进出境动植物检疫法
rules.statute_en: Law of the PRC on Entry and Exit Animal and Plant Quarantine
rules.rule: Seeds, seedlings and propagation material sent by post need prior quarantine approval; listed items are returned or destroyed.

rules.statute_en: Catalogue of Animals, Plants and Products Prohibited from Being Carried or Posted into the PRC (MARA/GACC Announcement No. 470)
rules.rule: Raw or cooked meat products, most aquatic products (dried/cooked excepted), dairy, eggs and non-canned bird's nest may not be posted in.

rules.statute_en: Catalogue of Animals, Plants and Products Prohibited from Being Carried or Posted into the PRC (MARA/GACC Announcement No. 470)

rules.statute: 中华人民共和国进出境动植物检疫法
rules.statute_en: Law of the PRC on Entry and Exit Animal and Plant Quarantine
rules.rule: Unlisted animal/plant products (e.g. tea, dried goods) are quarantined at the international mail exchange and released only if they pass.

rules.rule: No cosmetics-specific personal-parcel restriction found; own-use, reasonable quantity and the RMB 2,000 parcel limit apply.

rules.statute_en: Customs Law of the PRC

rules.rule: No device-specific personal-parcel restriction found; own-use and the RMB 2,000 parcel limit apply.

rules.statute_en: PRC Lists of Goods Prohibited / Restricted from Entry and Exit (Customs Order No. 43)

Current status not stated on the official page.
