rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: No Electronic Export Information filing is needed when each Schedule B/HTS line shipped to one consignee is worth $2,500 or less, unless another rule requires it.

rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: EEI must be filed regardless of value, including for exports by mail, when the item needs a licence or goes to a Country Group E:1/E:2 destination.

rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: General Prohibition Six: items subject to the EAR may not go to embargoed countries or regions without a licence or a licence exception specific to that destination.

rules.statute: USPS Publication 52 — Hazardous, Restricted, and Perishable Mail
rules.rule: Almost all dangerous goods are barred from international mail: explosives, gases, flammable liquids and solids, oxidizers, toxics, corrosives, dry ice, strong magnets and most Class 9 items.

rules.statute: USPS Publication 52 — Hazardous, Restricted, and Perishable Mail
rules.rule: Anything nonmailable domestically is also barred internationally, and each destination may add its own bans; senders must check the country list in the International Mail Manual.

rules.statute: USPS Publication 52 — Hazardous, Restricted, and Perishable Mail
rules.rule: Most live or dead animals cannot go by international mail; only bees, leeches, silkworms, Drosophila flies, dried insects or reptiles and certain beneficial insects may, where the destination allows.

rules.statute: Fish and Wildlife Service regulations (50 CFR Part 14)
rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Wildlife, including parts and products, may be imported or exported only through a designated Customs port of entry unless an exception applies.

rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Exporting or re-exporting any specimen of a CITES Appendix I, II or III species is unlawful unless the CITES permit and document requirements are met.

rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: U.S. law does not require plant export certification; APHIS issues phytosanitary certificates as a service when the importing country requires one.

rules.statute: USPS Publication 52 — Hazardous, Restricted, and Perishable Mail
rules.rule: Plants, seeds, fruits and vegetables sent abroad by mail must meet domestic plant-mailing rules and the destination country's quarantine regulations.

rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Exporting specimens of CITES-listed plant species, including seeds or parts where covered, requires CITES documents.

rules.statute: Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act
rules.rule: Food made for export is not treated as adulterated or misbranded if it meets the foreign buyer's specifications and destination law, is labeled for export on the outer package, and is not sold domestically.

rules.statute: USPS Publication 52 — Hazardous, Restricted, and Perishable Mail
rules.rule: Fresh meat, fruit, vegetables and other items likely to spoil in transit are nonmailable internationally.

rules.statute: Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act
rules.rule: Cosmetics intended for export escape U.S. adulteration and misbranding rules if made to the foreign buyer's specifications, legal at destination, labeled for export and not sold in the U.S.

rules.statute: USPS Publication 52 — Hazardous, Restricted, and Perishable Mail
rules.rule: Flammable liquids such as alcohol-based perfumes and nail polish are Class 3 dangerous goods and may not be sent by international mail.

rules.statute: USPS Publication 52 — Hazardous, Restricted, and Perishable Mail
rules.rule: Lithium batteries may go by international mail only when installed in the device: at most 4 cells or 2 batteries, lithium-ion up to 100 Wh per battery, lithium metal up to 2 g, no lithium marks.

rules.statute: USPS Publication 52 — Hazardous, Restricted, and Perishable Mail
rules.rule: Loose lithium batteries, batteries packed with but not installed in equipment, and used, damaged, defective or recalled batteries or devices are barred from international mail.

rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Small lithium cells and batteries shipped by carrier get relief from full hazmat rules only within size limits (20 Wh cell / 100 Wh battery for lithium-ion) and packaging and marking conditions.

rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Consumer wireless and other encryption items meeting the mass-market note are self-classified as 5A992/5D992 and lose national-security and encryption controls, though embargo and end-use rules still apply.
All spirits, wine, beer and other intoxicating liquors are nonmailable and may not be sent through the U.S. mail.

rules.statute: USPS Publication 52 — Hazardous, Restricted, and Perishable Mail
rules.rule: Intoxicating liquor, being nonmailable domestically, is also prohibited in international mail.
Cigarettes, roll-your-own and smokeless tobacco are nonmailable, and the limited PACT Act exceptions do not cover international mail. Cigars are outside this ban.

rules.statute: USPS Publication 52 — Hazardous, Restricted, and Perishable Mail
rules.rule: E-cigarettes, vape pens and any ENDS part, liquid or accessory, with or without nicotine, are nonmailable, and no exception applies to international mail.

rules.statute: USPS Publication 52 — Hazardous, Restricted, and Perishable Mail
rules.rule: Non-controlled drugs that are mailable domestically may be sent internationally unless the destination country bans them.

rules.statute: USPS Publication 52 — Hazardous, Restricted, and Perishable Mail
rules.rule: Controlled substances are not permitted in international mail.

rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Exporting Schedule I–II and most narcotic controlled substances requires DEA registration plus a per-shipment export permit; other scheduled substances need an export declaration.

rules.statute: Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act
rules.rule: Devices made for export follow the foreign buyer's specifications and destination law, but devices that miss certain U.S. requirements need extra FDA export conditions before shipment.

rules.statute: Rough Diamonds Control Regulations (31 CFR Part 592)
rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Rough diamonds may be exported only if controlled through the Kimberley Process Certification Scheme.

rules.statute: Bank Secrecy Act regulations (31 CFR Chapter X)
rules.agency: FinCEN / U.S. Customs and Border Protection
rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Anyone who mails or ships currency or monetary instruments totalling over $10,000 at one time out of the U.S. must file a report.

rules.statute: Safeguard Tribal Objects of Patrimony Act
rules.rule: Exporting Native American cultural items that are prohibited from exportation, or conspiring or concealing such export, is unlawful.

rules.statute: USPS Publication 52 — Hazardous, Restricted, and Perishable Mail
rules.rule: Rifles, pistols, revolvers (except pre-1898 of .50 calibre or less), short-barrel shotguns and automatic weapons may not be sent by international mail.

rules.statute: International Traffic in Arms Regulations (22 CFR Parts 120-130)
rules.page_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-10-29
rules.rule: Exports of defense articles and services are controlled under the Arms Export Control Act and need State Department authorization.
Switchblade and gravity knives that open automatically are nonmailable.

rules.statute: USPS Publication 52 — Hazardous, Restricted, and Perishable Mail
rules.rule: Replica or inert military ordnance, ammunition, shells and grenades are prohibited in international mail.

rules.statute: 18 U.S.C. 2320 — Trafficking in counterfeit goods or services
rules.rule: Knowingly trafficking in goods bearing counterfeit marks is a federal crime; trafficking expressly includes importing or exporting for commercial gain.

By post, jewellery, watches, precious stones, and platinum, gold or silver of more than nominal value may go abroad only by Priority Mail International, or First-Class Mail International with Registered Mail where customs treats it as a document; never Priority Mail Express International.
By post, any rough diamond may be mailed out of the United States only if controlled through the Kimberley Process Certification Scheme; otherwise its export by mail is prohibited.

By post, cigarettes, roll-your-own tobacco, smokeless tobacco and electronic nicotine delivery systems are nonmailable in outbound or inbound international mail, with no Publication 52 exceptions; cigars and pipe tobacco are not named.
Commercial goods worth under CAD 2,000 may be exported without an export report unless they are restricted goods or an officer asks for one.
All exported goods must be reported at the prescribed time, place and manner, subject to the regulatory exemptions.
Goods or technology on the Export Control List, or any goods bound for a country on the Area Control List, need an export permit.
Dangerous goods under the Transportation of Dangerous Goods rules, and items barred by the Universal Postal Convention, are non-mailable unless Canada Post accepts them under those rules.
Any item sent by post in breach of a Canadian Act or regulation is non-mailable.
Live animals are non-mailable unless covered by an agreement with Canada Post or listed in the Postal Guide (such as bees, leeches, small cold-blooded animals) and properly packed.
Livestock, poultry and animal germplasm may be exported only with proof they meet the importing country's sanitary rules and a CFIA-endorsed export certificate.

rules.statute: Wild Animal and Plant Protection and Regulation of International and Interprovincial Trade Act
rules.rule: Regulated wild animals, or their parts or derivatives, may be exported only under a permit (CITES species).
Mailing plants, seeds, fruit, bark, plant parts and soil is regulated under the Plant Protection Act and CITES; the CFIA permit office handles questions.

rules.statute: Wild Animal and Plant Protection and Regulation of International and Interprovincial Trade Act
rules.rule: Regulated wild plants, or their parts or derivatives, may be exported only under a permit (CITES species).
Packaged food made in Canada only for export is exempt from most of the Act if it has a certificate showing it meets the destination country's law, though core safety sections still apply.
Food an individual exports, not for business and within CFIA's maximum personal-use quantities, counts as personal use and is exempt from licensing.
Fish, game, meat, fruit, vegetables and other perishables are non-mailable unless packed to Canada Postal Guide requirements.
Cosmetics made only for export are exempt from most of the Act with a certificate of compliance with destination law, but the bans on injurious or unsanitary cosmetics still apply.
Highly flammable or otherwise dangerous contents, such as alcohol-based perfumes and aerosols that are dangerous goods, cannot be mailed.
Lithium batteries may not be mailed to any destination outside Canada and the United States.
Lithium batteries may go to the U.S. only under Transportation of Dangerous Goods Special Provision 34 and Canada Post's packing table, with a fully completed customs declaration.
Radio or crypto-enabled equipment listed on the Export Control List needs an export permit; unlisted consumer devices do not.
Intoxicating beverages may be mailed abroad only if export requirements are met and the destination postal administration accepts them.
Only the licensee responsible for bulk alcohol, or listed licensed parties, may export bulk spirits or wine.
Vaping products are non-mailable unless sent by a ground service and any lithium battery meets Canada Post's ground-mail rules.
Substances in Schedules I to VI may not be exported from Canada except as authorized by the regulations.
Drugs, narcotics and controlled substances may be mailed only in certain circumstances under the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act and Food and Drugs Act.
Devices made in Canada only for export are exempt from most of the Act with a certificate that they meet the destination country's law.

rules.statute: Export and Import of Rough Diamonds Act
rules.rule: Rough diamonds must be exported in a compliant container with a Canadian Kimberley Process Certificate, and the export must be reported.
Gold bullion, gold dust and non-manufactured precious metals are non-mailable unless under an agreement with Canada Post.

rules.statute: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act; Cross-border Currency and Monetary Instruments Reporting Regulations
rules.rule: Exporting currency or bearer monetary instruments worth CAD 10,000 or more, including by mail or courier, must be reported to the CBSA.

rules.statute: Cultural Property Export and Import Act
rules.rule: Objects on the Canadian Cultural Property Export Control List may not be exported without a cultural property export permit.
Firearms, including imitation and replica firearms, may never be mailed internationally; ammunition is prohibited in the mail.
Exporting firearms, prohibited or restricted weapons, devices, firearm parts or prohibited ammunition without authorization under the Firearms Act or other federal law is an offence.
Replica or inert munitions and devices that imitate explosives, including display grenades, are non-mailable.
Goods, labels or packaging bearing an unauthorized mark identical or essentially identical to a registered trademark may not be exported, except small personal-use amounts carried by an individual.
Infringing copies of copyright works made without the owner's consent may not be exported, apart from personal-use copies in an individual's baggage.

rules.statute: Customs (Export) procedures as set out in HMRC guidance (Taxation (Cross-border Trade) Act 2018)
rules.article: n/a (HMRC guidance: Making a full export declaration)
rules.rule: Goods leaving the UK need an export declaration and customs clearance before they depart; it must list commodity code, value, consignee and any licences or certificates.

rules.statute: VAT Notice 703: VAT on goods exported from the UK
rules.rule: Postal exports can be zero-rated for VAT only with proof of posting to a non-UK address; Parcelforce parcels each need a full, accurate customs declaration describing contents, quantity, weight and value.

rules.statute: VAT Notice 703: VAT on goods exported from the UK
rules.rule: For courier and fast-parcel exports the seller must keep evidence linking the specific consignment to its export, since couriers rarely issue separate shipping certificates.

rules.statute: Export goods from the UK: step by step (HMRC/DBT guidance)
rules.rule: Special licences or certificates may be required to export animals, plants, medicines, medical devices, chemicals, diamonds, cultural goods, firearms, military and dual-use items; an EORI number starting GB is also needed.
Sending by post any item likely to injure mail or postal workers is an offence unless the postal operator permits it; covers dangerous goods such as unpermitted batteries or flammables.

rules.statute: Export live animals: special rules (Defra/APHA guidance)
rules.rule: Exporting live animals from Great Britain requires an export health certificate; EU-bound animals must be checked at an EU border control post with 24 hours advance notice.

rules.statute: CITES as applied in GB (Control of Trade in Endangered Species Regulations)
rules.rule: Exports or re-exports of CITES-listed animals, plants or their parts and products need a CITES permit or certificate issued by APHA.

Plants, seeds and plant products may need a phytosanitary certificate depending on the destination country; exporters check the destination requirements and apply to APHA for certificates and inspections.

rules.statute: Export food and drink rules (Defra/APHA guidance)
rules.rule: Food or drink containing products of animal origin generally needs an export health certificate; plain processed food without animal products usually does not, though some non-EU buyers require a certificate of free sale.
Exporting a controlled drug is prohibited unless an exemption applies or it is done under a Home Office licence and its conditions.

rules.statute: Export drugs and medicines: special rules (GOV.UK guidance)
rules.rule: Exporting human or veterinary medicines needs the relevant manufacturer, wholesale dealer and marketing licences; controlled drugs need an additional Home Office export licence.

rules.statute: Human Medicines Regulations 2012 (restricted medicines list, DHSC)
rules.rule: Medicines placed on the UK market for UK patients that appear on the restricted medicines list must not be exported or hoarded by wholesale dealers.

rules.statute: Export medical devices: special rules (MHRA guidance)
rules.rule: Some destination countries require a Certificate of Free Sale for medical devices; MHRA issues it only for devices registered in its DORS system by a UK manufacturer or UK responsible person.
Jewellery, gold and precious metals can be exported without a licence, except rough diamonds; precious stones, gold and silver goods may not go to North Korea or Syria.
Each export of uncut rough diamonds needs a Kimberley Process certificate and may only go to KP participant countries, otherwise goods may be seized.
Exporting precious and semi-precious stones, gold and silver items and other luxury goods to North Korea is banned.
Exporting ivory from the UK for sale or hire counts as prohibited dealing in ivory, unless a statutory exemption applies.
Cash of £10,000 or more carried between Great Britain and a non-UK country must be declared; Border Force may seize any cash suspected of criminal links.

rules.statute: Export of Objects of Cultural Interest (Control) Order 2003
rules.rule: Objects within the cultural-interest controls may only be exported from the UK under a written licence from the Secretary of State; Arts Council England administers applications.

rules.statute: Export art, antiques and cultural goods: special rules (GOV.UK guidance)
rules.rule: A UK export licence is needed to send qualifying cultural objects from Great Britain to any place outside the UK; the licence copy is attached to the export declaration.
Firearms, their parts, accessories and ammunition are controlled strategic goods; exporting them without the correct licence is a criminal offence.
Selling, offering or distributing goods bearing an unauthorised registered trade mark for gain is a criminal offence, which covers counterfeit goods shipped to overseas buyers.

rules.statute: Royal Mail and Parcelforce Worldwide prohibited and restricted items (carrier rule, personal customer guidelines)
rules.rule: By post, Royal Mail and Parcelforce refuse alcoholic drinks above 24% ABV (spirits such as gin, rum, vodka, whisky) for international destinations; liquids above 70% ABV are refused in all mail.

rules.statute: Royal Mail and Parcelforce Worldwide prohibited and restricted items (carrier rule, personal customer guidelines)
rules.article: A-Z list: Alcohol (24% ABV or less)
rules.rule: By post, beer, wine and other drinks of 24% ABV or less may be sent abroad only if sealed in polythene, cushioned with absorbent material, glass marked FRAGILE, sender address shown.

rules.statute: Royal Mail and Parcelforce Worldwide prohibited and restricted items (carrier rule, personal customer guidelines)
rules.rule: By post, perfumes, aftershaves, eau de toilette, non-aerosol body sprays and essential oils are not accepted for international destinations; non-flammable perfumed creams, gels, oils and lotions are excluded from this ban.

rules.statute: Royal Mail and Parcelforce Worldwide prohibited and restricted items (carrier rule, personal customer guidelines)
rules.article: A-Z list: Nail varnish, polish or gel
rules.rule: By post, nail varnish, polish or gel (solvent or water based) is not accepted for international destinations; UK-only sending is allowed with limits.

rules.statute: Royal Mail and Parcelforce Worldwide prohibited and restricted items (carrier rule, personal customer guidelines)
rules.rule: By post, toiletry and medicinal aerosols such as deodorants, body sprays, hair sprays and shaving foams are not accepted for international destinations; other aerosols are refused in all mail.

rules.statute: Royal Mail and Parcelforce Worldwide prohibited and restricted items (carrier rule, personal customer guidelines)
rules.rule: By post, e-cigarettes may be sent to international destinations only when securely packed against movement; devices containing batteries must also meet the battery rules.

rules.statute: Royal Mail and Parcelforce Worldwide prohibited and restricted items (carrier rule, personal customer guidelines)
rules.rule: By post, e-cigarette nicotine solutions with more than 2% nicotine concentration are refused for UK and international destinations.

rules.statute: Royal Mail and Parcelforce Worldwide prohibited and restricted items (carrier rule, personal customer guidelines)
rules.article: A-Z list: Nicotine Solution (2% or less)
rules.rule: By post, e-liquids with 2% nicotine or less may go abroad only if they comply with the Tobacco and Related Products Regulations 2016 and are sealed in a leak-proof liner and leak-proof outer packaging.

rules.statute: Royal Mail and Parcelforce Worldwide prohibited and restricted items (carrier rule, personal customer guidelines)
rules.article: A-Z list: Batteries (not with equipment / ICAO dangerous goods)
rules.rule: By post, loose lithium batteries, power banks, spillable lead-acid batteries, used alkaline, NiMH, NiCd or zinc-air batteries and damaged batteries of any type are refused for UK and international destinations.

rules.statute: Royal Mail and Parcelforce Worldwide prohibited and restricted items (carrier rule, personal customer guidelines)
rules.article: A-Z list: Lithium ion/polymer or lithium metal batteries sent with equipment
rules.rule: By post, lithium-ion or lithium-metal batteries packed alongside, not installed in, a device are not accepted for international destinations; UK-only sending is allowed with limits.

rules.statute: Royal Mail and Parcelforce Worldwide prohibited and restricted items (carrier rule, personal customer guidelines)
rules.article: A-Z list: Lithium ion/polymer batteries contained in equipment
rules.rule: By post, devices with installed lithium-ion batteries may go abroad if batteries are undamaged, UN 38.3 tested, short-circuit protected and the device is rigidly packed against activation.

rules.statute: Royal Mail and Parcelforce Worldwide prohibited and restricted items (carrier rule, personal customer guidelines)
rules.article: A-Z list: Alkaline, NiMH, NiCd, zinc-air and zinc chloride batteries without equipment
rules.rule: By post, alkaline, NiMH, NiCd, zinc-air and zinc chloride batteries sent without a device may go abroad only new, unopened in original retail packaging and cushioned.
Parcels to non-EU countries need no export declaration if goods are non-commercial or commercial worth at most €1,000, not subject to licences, bans or refund claims.

rules.statute: Zollkodex der Union (Ausfuhrverfahren), per Zoll guidance
rules.rule: Above €1,000 or for licensed goods, an electronic ATLAS export declaration is required; the export accompanying document travels with Deutsche Post parcels under a yellow export label.
Postal parcels sent under the Universal Postal Convention must carry a CN22 or CN23 customs content declaration stating value and contents.
DHL accepts high-value parcel contents only up to €25,000 per parcel; higher values are never permitted.

rules.statute: AGB DHL Paket International / AGB Brief International (Gefahrgut)
rules.rule: Dangerous goods, which can include batteries and accumulators, aerosols, cleaning agents and perfume, are excluded from international DHL parcels; private customers cannot ship them abroad.
Perfume and aerosol cosmetics that qualify as dangerous goods cannot be sent internationally by private DHL customers.
Endangered-species rules and documents apply in full to postal and courier exports; travellers personal-item exemptions do not apply to parcels.
Dual-use items, including sensitive electronics, telecoms and IT goods and software, may need an export authorisation before shipment outside the EU.
Each import or export of narcotics needs, in addition to the § 3 licence, a permit from the Federal Institute for Drugs and Medical Devices (BfArM).
Shipping rough diamonds outside the EU requires a Kimberley certificate after physical inspection by the competent authority; no value or quantity exemption exists.

rules.statute: AGB DHL Paket (zulässige Inhalte, Valoren Klasse II)
rules.rule: Precious metals such as gold or silver bars, nuggets and bullion coins are limited to €500 per DHL parcel; jewellery and watches may go internationally up to €25,000.

rules.statute: AGB DHL Paket (zulässige Inhalte, Valoren Klasse II)
rules.rule: Valid banknotes and coins in any currency may be sent in a DHL parcel only up to €500.
For unaccompanied cash of €10,000 or more sent across the border, customs may require the sender or recipient to file a disclosure within 30 days.
Exporting cultural goods to a non-EU country requires a licence under Regulation (EC) No 116/2009, subject to its age and value thresholds.
National cultural property needs a licence to leave Germany, and items whose listing as nationally valuable is pending may not be exported.
Moving weapons or ammunition out of Germany needs a permit; postal shipping must be cleared in advance with the weapons authority or BAFA.

rules.statute: Gesetz über die Kontrolle von Kriegswaffen (KrWaffKontrG)
rules.rule: War weapons may only be imported, exported or transited when the related transport is approved or covered by a general licence.
Goods unlawfully bearing a protected trade mark can be seized by customs on export or import at the right holder request, unless Regulation (EU) 608/2013 applies.

rules.statute: Zoll guidance: Einschränkungen (Waren) for postal exports to non-EU states
rules.rule: Zoll's list of goods restricted for postal export to non-EU states covers only species protection, dual-use goods, torture goods, rough diamonds, cultural goods and weapons. No national export restriction on alcohol found; destination and carrier rules apply.

rules.statute: Zoll guidance: Einschränkungen (Waren) for postal exports to non-EU states
rules.rule: Zoll's list of goods restricted for postal export to non-EU states covers only species protection, dual-use goods, torture goods, rough diamonds, cultural goods and weapons. No national export restriction on tobacco products found; destination and carrier rules apply.

rules.statute: Zoll guidance: Einschränkungen (Waren) for postal exports to non-EU states
rules.rule: Zoll's list of goods restricted for postal export to non-EU states covers only species protection, dual-use goods, torture goods, rough diamonds, cultural goods and weapons. No national export restriction on e-cigarettes or refill liquids found; destination and carrier rules apply.

rules.statute: Zoll guidance: Einschränkungen (Waren) for postal exports to non-EU states
rules.rule: Apart from species-protection (CITES) documents, Zoll's postal-export restriction list names no national rule for live animals. Destination animal-health requirements and carrier rules apply.

rules.agency: Bundesamt für Justiz (Gesetzestext); Pflanzenschutzdienste der Länder
rules.rule: If the destination country requires a phytosanitary certificate, plants, plant products and seeds may only be exported with one issued to the exporter. Authorities may inspect and block exports failing destination plant-health rules.
Goods, including mail items, worth more than AUD 2,000 or needing an export permit must be entered on an Export Declaration; lower-value goods are exempt. Australia charges no export duty.

rules.statute: Australia Post General Terms and Conditions
rules.rule: Australia Post will not carry dangerous goods such as flammable liquids (nail polish, paint, perfume), flammable solids, aerosols, explosives, ammunition and corrosives, domestically or overseas.
Goods covered by Australian autonomous sanctions cannot be exported to sanctioned countries or entities without permission.
Items sent overseas must also be accepted by the destination's customs; Australia Post points senders to its International Post Guide for country rules.

rules.statute: Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999
rules.agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
rules.rule: Australian native animals and their products need a DCCEEW export permit; exempt-listed specimens can go without one, but never live native animals.

rules.statute: Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999
rules.agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
rules.rule: CITES-listed animals and products made from them need a CITES export permit from DCCEEW.

rules.agency: Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry
rules.rule: Live animals, including cats, dogs and other companion animals, are prescribed export goods controlled by DAFF and need government export clearance.
Domestic cat and dog fur and goods containing it cannot be exported without permission.

rules.agency: Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry
rules.rule: Cut flowers, foliage, fresh fruit and vegetables, grains and seeds, hay, processed plant products and timber are prescribed export goods under DAFF control.

rules.statute: Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999
rules.agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
rules.rule: Australian native plants and CITES-listed plants need a DCCEEW export permit; live native plants are never exempt.

rules.agency: Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry
rules.rule: Dairy, eggs and egg products, fish and fish products, and meat products are prescribed export goods requiring DAFF controls such as registered establishments and certificates.

rules.agency: Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry
rules.rule: Highly processed foods such as wine usually leave without government export controls, unless the importing country asks for certification.
Toothfish exports need permission under the export regulations.

rules.article: GMP certificate for cosmetics exported to China
rules.agency: Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry
rules.rule: For cosmetics registered in China, DAFF can issue a certificate confirming good manufacturing practice, backed by a TGA licence or ISO 22716 evidence.

rules.statute: Australia Post General Terms and Conditions
rules.rule: Australia Post takes lithium-ion batteries up to 20 Wh per cell or 100 Wh per battery and lithium-metal up to 1 g per cell or 2 g per battery. Overseas, they must be installed in the device, at most two batteries or four cells.

rules.statute: Australia Post General Terms and Conditions
rules.rule: Australia Post will not send lithium batteries to Bhutan, Germany, Italy, Laos, Macao or Thailand, will not post loose or recalled batteries, and will not accept lithium-powered electronics on International Courier.
Goods on the Defence and Strategic Goods List, including dual-use technology, cannot be exported without Defence permission.
Consignments of wine, brandy, grape spirit or wine products over 100 litres need Wine Australia export approval under its licensing conditions.
PBS-subsidised medicines may only be sent abroad in reasonable amounts for personal treatment, with a PBS Medicine Export Declaration; an Office of Drug Control permit may also apply.
Drugs listed in Schedule 8 of the export regulations cannot be exported without a permit.
Exporting a medical device that is not included in the Australian Register of Therapeutic Goods is a criminal offence unless an exemption or approval applies.
Rough diamonds can only be exported under the Kimberley Process certification rules.

rules.statute: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2006
rules.rule: Moving monetary instruments worth AUD 10,000 or more out of Australia, including by mail or courier, must be reported; commercial carriers carrying for others are excused.

rules.statute: Protection of Movable Cultural Heritage Act 1986
rules.rule: Australian protected objects, such as significant Aboriginal heritage items, archaeological objects, fossils, meteorites and historical documents, cannot be exported without a permit.
Firearms, military goods and other items on the Defence and Strategic Goods List cannot be exported without Defence permission.

rules.statute: Australia Post General Terms and Conditions
rules.rule: Australia Post will not carry explosives such as flares, fireworks or ammunition.
Exporting counterfeit credit, debit or charge cards is prohibited without written permission.
Exporting wine whose description and presentation are false is an offence.

rules.statute_en: Customs Act (JP)
rules.agency: Japan Customs (MOF Customs and Tariff Bureau)
rules.rule: Postal items valued at JPY 200,000 or less leave Japan without an export declaration (a customs label is enough); items above JPY 200,000 need a formal export declaration, filed by the sender or a customs broker.

rules.statute_en: Customs Act (JP)
rules.agency: Japan Customs (MOF Customs and Tariff Bureau)
rules.rule: Goods needing a permit or approval under other laws (trade control, cultural property, quarantine, narcotics, wildlife) must show that approval to customs; otherwise export is refused, including postal items checked at the exchange office.

rules.statute: 国際郵便として送れないもの（日本郵便：万国郵便条約・航空危険物規則等に基づく禁制品）
rules.statute_en: Japan Post: items that cannot be sent by international mail
rules.article: あて先の国によって送れないもの
rules.rule: Besides the worldwide postal ban list, each destination has its own prohibited items; Japan Post says meat, fruit, vegetables, liquor and tobacco are frequently refused, so check the destination list before mailing.

rules.statute: 国際郵便として送れないもの（日本郵便：万国郵便条約・航空危険物規則等に基づく禁制品）
rules.statute_en: Japan Post: items that cannot be sent by international mail
rules.rule: Live animals cannot be sent by international mail from Japan.

rules.statute_en: Rabies Prevention Act (JP)
rules.rule: Dogs, cats, raccoons, foxes and skunks may only be exported after animal quarantine inspection.

rules.statute_en: Act on Domestic Animal Infectious Diseases Control (JP)
rules.rule: Animals and animal products that the importing country requires to be certified, or that MAFF designates, must pass export inspection by an animal quarantine officer and carry an export quarantine certificate.

rules.statute_en: Export Trade Control Order (JP)
rules.article: 第2条・別表第二（三六の項）
rules.rule: Specimens of CITES Appendix I or II species, including parts, eggs, seeds, taxidermy and processed goods, need METI export approval for any destination.

rules.statute_en: Plant Protection Act (JP)
rules.rule: Plants and plant products bound for a country that requires a Japanese phytosanitary certificate must be inspected by a plant protection officer and certified before export.

rules.statute_en: Act on Domestic Animal Infectious Diseases Control (JP)
rules.rule: Meat, sausages, ham and other animal products that the destination requires to be certified, or that MAFF designates, need an export quarantine certificate before shipping.

rules.statute: 国際郵便として送れないもの（日本郵便：万国郵便条約・航空危険物規則等に基づく禁制品）
rules.statute_en: Japan Post: items that cannot be sent by international mail
rules.article: あて先の国によって送れないもの
rules.rule: Many destinations bar meat, fruit and vegetables by post; Japan Post warns that foods such as cup noodles, curry or consommé can be refused where beef is banned, and even packaging printed with meat or produce can be rejected.

rules.statute: 国際郵便として送れないもの（日本郵便：万国郵便条約・航空危険物規則等に基づく禁制品）
rules.statute_en: Japan Post: items that cannot be sent by international mail
rules.article: 航空危険物（引火性液体・高圧ガス）
rules.rule: Perfume, nail polish, aerosol sprays, and sunscreen or hair tonic with more than 24% alcohol are air dangerous goods and cannot be sent by international mail, even by surface.

rules.statute: 国際郵便として送れないもの（日本郵便：万国郵便条約・航空危険物規則等に基づく禁制品）
rules.statute_en: Japan Post: items that cannot be sent by international mail
rules.rule: Items covered by the IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations cannot be sent by international mail by any service or route: fireworks, lighter fuel, gas cylinders, matches, lighters, bleach, pesticides, mercury, wet batteries, dry ice.

rules.statute: 国際郵便として送れないもの（日本郵便：万国郵便条約・航空危険物規則等に基づく禁制品）
rules.statute_en: Japan Post: items that cannot be sent by international mail
rules.article: リチウム電池（単体・同梱）
rules.rule: Loose lithium batteries, batteries packed with but not fitted in equipment, and power banks cannot be sent by international mail.

rules.statute: 国際郵便として送れないもの（日本郵便：万国郵便条約・航空危険物規則等に基づく禁制品）
rules.statute_en: Japan Post: items that cannot be sent by international mail
rules.article: リチウム電池の郵送条件
rules.rule: Lithium batteries fitted inside equipment may be mailed only if protected from short circuit, within lithium or watt-hour limits, at most four cells or two batteries, and to destinations that accept them.

rules.statute: 国際郵便として送れないもの（日本郵便：万国郵便条約・航空危険物規則等に基づく禁制品）
rules.statute_en: Japan Post: items that cannot be sent by international mail
rules.article: 航空危険物（アルコール飲料）
rules.rule: Alcoholic beverages stronger than 24% alcohol cannot be sent by international mail.

rules.statute: 国際郵便として送れないもの（日本郵便：万国郵便条約・航空危険物規則等に基づく禁制品）
rules.statute_en: Japan Post: items that cannot be sent by international mail
rules.article: 送るものにより特別な条件が適用されるもの
rules.rule: Alcoholic beverages at or below 24% may be mailed only under Japan Post's special conditions for liquor, which differ from domestic Yu-Pack rules, and only where the destination allows them.

rules.statute: 国際郵便として送れないもの（日本郵便：万国郵便条約・航空危険物規則等に基づく禁制品）
rules.statute_en: Japan Post: items that cannot be sent by international mail
rules.article: あて先の国によって送れないもの
rules.rule: Japan does not bar tobacco exports by post, but Japan Post lists tobacco among items most often prohibited by destination countries.

rules.statute: 国際郵便として送れないもの（日本郵便：万国郵便条約・航空危険物規則等に基づく禁制品）
rules.statute_en: Japan Post: items that cannot be sent by international mail
rules.article: 航空危険物（その他の有害物件）
rules.rule: Electronic cigarettes are listed as air dangerous goods and cannot be sent by international mail.

rules.statute_en: Customs Act (JP)
rules.agency: Japan Customs (MOF Customs and Tariff Bureau)
rules.rule: Narcotics, psychotropics, cannabis, opium, poppy straw and stimulants (including precursors) may not be exported, except by the government or licensed persons.

rules.statute: 国際郵便として送れないもの（日本郵便：万国郵便条約・航空危険物規則等に基づく禁制品）
rules.statute_en: Japan Post: items that cannot be sent by international mail
rules.rule: Gold, silver, platinum, gems and other valuables cannot go by EMS; other parcel or letter services accept them only registered or insured, subject to destination bans and value caps. Registered small packets stopped taking them after 2025-12-31.

rules.statute: 国際郵便として送れないもの（日本郵便：万国郵便条約・航空危険物規則等に基づく禁制品）
rules.statute_en: Japan Post: items that cannot be sent by international mail
rules.rule: Coins, banknotes, bearer securities and traveller's cheques cannot go by EMS; other postal services accept them only registered or insured, where the destination allows.

rules.statute_en: Foreign Exchange Order (JP)
rules.rule: The advance report to the Finance Minister for cash or securities above JPY 1 million (or precious metals above the set weight) applies when carried in person; other export modes are exempt under this order.

rules.statute_en: Act on Protection of Cultural Properties (JP)
rules.rule: Designated Important Cultural Properties may not be exported unless the Commissioner for Cultural Affairs grants permission.

rules.statute: 外国為替及び外国貿易法
rules.statute_en: Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Act (JP)
rules.rule: Goods listed by cabinet order, including weapons, need a METI export licence for the listed destinations.

rules.statute: 国際郵便として送れないもの（日本郵便：万国郵便条約・航空危険物規則等に基づく禁制品）
rules.statute_en: Japan Post: items that cannot be sent by international mail
rules.article: 刀剣等を内容品とする航空郵便物
rules.rule: Airmail containing swords, spears or halberds with blades 15 cm or longer, or daggers and switchblades 5.5 cm or longer, must carry Japan Post's weapons label; it travels slower and may be returned if no airline will carry it.

rules.statute: 国際郵便として送れないもの（日本郵便：万国郵便条約・航空危険物規則等に基づく禁制品）
rules.statute_en: Japan Post: items that cannot be sent by international mail
rules.rule: Ammunition, fireworks and party crackers are explosives under the dangerous goods rules and cannot be sent by international mail.

rules.statute_en: Customs Act (JP)
rules.article: 第69条の2第1項第3号・第4号
rules.agency: Japan Customs (MOF Customs and Tariff Bureau)
rules.rule: Goods infringing patents, utility models, designs, trademarks, copyright, neighbouring rights or plant breeder rights, and goods constituting specified unfair competition, may not be exported; customs may confiscate and destroy them.

rules.statute: 輸出貿易管理令 (Export Trade Control Order) under 外国為替及び外国貿易法 Art. 48(1)
rules.agency: 経済産業省 (METI); e-Gov法令検索
rules.rule: Transmission telecom equipment, electronic switching gear, optical fibre, phased-array antennas, direction finders, interception or jamming devices and internet-monitoring equipment meeting METI specifications need a METI export licence, to all destinations.

rules.statute: Regulation of Imports and Exports Act 1995
rules.rule: Parcel post may leave Singapore without a customs export permit, as may air exports of S$1,000 or less, unless the goods are dutiable or controlled; then a permit is required.

rules.statute: Regulation of Imports and Exports Act 1995
rules.rule: Controlled goods need authorisation (advance notification, licence or certificate) from the competent authority before export; check the HS/CA product code checker. UN Security Council sanctions also apply.

rules.statute: Regulation of Imports and Exports Act 1995
rules.rule: Rhinoceros horn, worked or unworked, including any part, powder or waste, cannot be exported from Singapore.
No animal or bird may be exported without a licence from the Director-General.

CITES-listed animals and plants, including parts and derivatives, need a CITES permit before leaving Singapore; this applies to individuals as well as businesses, and to personal ivory items each trip.

rules.agency: Director-General under the Control of Plants Act
rules.rule: The Minister may prohibit export of specified plants, and plant exports needing certification travel with a phytosanitary certificate issued under the Act.

rules.statute: Regulation of Imports and Exports Act 1995
rules.rule: Every food export consignment needs a Cargo Clearance Permit from Singapore Customs, which carries SFA's requirements; meat and shell eggs also need an SFA export licence, and destination rules must be met.

rules.statute: SingPost General Prohibition & Dangerous Goods (carrier rule, IATA DG classes)
rules.rule: Perfume, nail polish and removers (flammable liquids) and hair or textile dyes (oxidisers) must not be shipped through SingPost.

rules.statute: SingPost General Prohibition & Dangerous Goods (carrier rule, IATA DG classes)
rules.rule: SingPost will not carry dangerous goods: explosives, compressed gas and aerosols, flammable liquids and solids, oxidisers, toxic substances, radioactive material, corrosives including wet or sealed lead-acid batteries, magnetised items, dry ice.

rules.statute: SingPost General Prohibition & Dangerous Goods (carrier rule, IATA DG classes)
rules.rule: Lithium batteries go only inside equipment, undamaged, in strong packaging, without a lithium battery mark, at most 4 cells or 2 batteries per package; lithium-ion up to 20 Wh per cell or 100 Wh per battery, lithium-metal up to 1 g or 2 g.

rules.statute: SingPost General Prohibition & Dangerous Goods (carrier rule, IATA DG classes)
rules.rule: SingPost lists alcohol among flammable liquids that must not be shipped.

rules.statute: Regulation of Imports and Exports Act 1995
rules.rule: Liquor is dutiable, so the parcel-post permit exemption does not apply; a customs export permit is required.

rules.statute: Regulation of Imports and Exports Act 1995
rules.rule: Tobacco products are dutiable, so exports need a customs export permit even when sent by parcel post.
Vaporisers and their nicotine solutions may not be imported, sold, bought, used or possessed in Singapore, so a seller cannot lawfully hold stock to export.

rules.statute: Corruption, Drug Trafficking and Other Serious Crimes (Confiscation of Benefits) Act 1992
rules.agency: Singapore Police Force (Suspicious Transaction Reporting Office)
rules.rule: Cross-border movements of physical currency and bearer negotiable instruments out of Singapore must be reported under Part 6A.
Military goods and related technology on the strategic goods control list need an export, transhipment or brokering permit from Singapore Customs.

rules.statute: SingPost General Prohibition & Dangerous Goods (carrier rule, IATA DG classes)
rules.rule: Ammunition, fireworks, flares and caps for toy firearms must not be shipped through SingPost.

Customs can seize goods about to be exported that are suspected of infringing a registered trade mark, copyright, geographical indication or registered design, on a rights holder's notice or on its own initiative.

rules.statute: Singapore Customs guidance: Controlled and Prohibited Goods for Exports; Strategic Goods (Control) Act
rules.rule: No radio-specific export rule found; IMDA TradeNet requirements cover imports. Controlled goods need competent-authority approval (check HS/CA code checker); strategic items need permits. Carrier rules apply.

rules.statute: Misuse of Drugs Act 1973; Misuse of Drugs Regulations
rules.rule: Exporting controlled drugs, other than First Schedule preparations, needs a controlled drugs export licence (CDEL) plus a controlled drugs wholesale licence (CDWL), held by a registered pharmacist.

rules.statute: Health Products (Therapeutic Products) Regulations 2016, per HSA guidance
rules.rule: Companies importing therapeutic products solely for export need an importer's licence (TPIL, restricted activity); a wholesaler's licence (TPWL) is not required for that activity.

rules.statute: Health Products Act 2007, per HSA guidance
rules.rule: Supplying, including exporting, unregistered medical devices is prohibited. Importing unregistered devices for re-export needs case-by-case HSA approval unless the dealer holds importer and wholesaler licences.

rules.statute: Health Products (Medical Devices) Regulations, per HSA guidance
rules.rule: A dealer's licence (manufacturer, importer or wholesaler) is required to manufacture, import or wholesale medical devices in Singapore; applications go through SHARE.
Exporters must lodge an export declaration within 14 days; postal packets whose contents are worth under HK$4,000 are exempt from declaration.
Articles listed in Schedule 2 of Cap. 60A (pesticides, medicines, Chinese medicines, rough diamonds, scheduled chemicals, powdered formula) need an export licence before leaving Hong Kong.
Nothing explosive, inflammable or dangerous, no live or dead animals or insects, no dangerous drugs, obscene items, or goods banned in Hong Kong or the destination may be sent by post.

Every outbound item is X-rayed; anything that cannot be confirmed as non-dangerous is opened and returned without postage refund. Liquids should travel in original packing with ingredients shown and an MSDS.

rules.statute: Hongkong Post customs clearance of outbound mail
rules.rule: Senders must fill in CN22 or CN23 customs forms in detail; destination customs may withhold, seize, return or charge duties on the item.
Strategic commodities such as high-performance computers, advanced integrated circuits, sophisticated communication systems and munitions need a TID licence for every export shipment.
Live or dead animals and insects may not be sent through the Hong Kong post, except as allowed by postal regulations.

rules.statute: Protection of Endangered Species of Animals and Plants Ordinance (Cap. 586)
rules.rule: Exporting CITES-listed animals, alive or dead, including parts and derivatives, needs an AFCD licence per shipment and inspection before export; wild Appendix I specimens cannot be traded commercially.

rules.article: s. 6D (live animals not listed in Cap. 60A Sch. 2)
rules.rule: Exporting non-endangered live animals is not licensed by Hong Kong, but the exporter must meet destination import rules; AFCD issues animal health certificates on request.

rules.statute: Protection of Endangered Species of Animals and Plants Ordinance (Cap. 586)
rules.rule: CITES-listed plants and their parts or derivatives need an AFCD export licence per shipment and must be inspected before export.
Hong Kong does not license ordinary plant or seed exports, but many destinations demand a phytosanitary certificate, which AFCD issues to exporters on application.
Powdered formula for children under 36 months cannot be exported without a licence; the only exemption is up to 1.8 kg carried in a departing traveller's own baggage, so parcels need a licence.

rules.statute: Reserved Commodities (Control of Imports, Exports and Reserve Stocks) Regulations (Cap. 296A)
rules.rule: Rice is a reserved commodity; re-exports need a TID export licence, except up to 15 kg in a traveller's personal luggage.

rules.statute: Conservation of Antarctic Marine Living Resources (Toothfish Catch Documentation Scheme) Regulation (Cap. 635A)
rules.rule: Toothfish items, fresh or processed, need an AFCD export or re-export licence, except up to 15 kg in personal baggage for own use or gifts.
Exporting regulated mercury-added products is banned, including cosmetics with mercury content above 1 ppm.

rules.article: s. 32(1)(b); Hongkong Post dangerous articles guidance
rules.rule: Hongkong Post does not accept lithium batteries; remove removable batteries before posting. Items with loose batteries, phones or equipment containing lithium batteries are treated as dangerous and returned.
Aerosols and pressurised containers, flammable liquids and products, and magnetized material count as dangerous articles and cannot be posted.

rules.article: Sch. 1 Munitions List; Dangerous Goods Ordinance (Cap. 295)
rules.rule: Explosives on the Munitions List need a TID export licence with prior endorsement, plus Dangerous Goods Ordinance controls.
Radio transmitting apparatus can only be exported under an OFCA permit unless the exporter holds a Radio Dealers Licence (Unrestricted).
Exporting dutiable liquor (spirits above 30% alcohol by volume) needs a Customs licence and removal permits.
Wine and other liquor of 30% alcohol by volume or less carry a 0% duty rate and are outside the liquor licensing requirement.
Exporting tobacco products needs a Customs licence and removal permits.
Importing and consigning smokeless tobacco products is banned in Hong Kong.

Selling, offering for sale, manufacturing, or holding alternative smoking products (e-cigarettes, heated tobacco, herbal cigarettes) for sale is banned, so a Hong Kong seller cannot lawfully sell them abroad.
Pharmaceutical products and medicines need a Department of Health export licence; only reasonable personal quantities carried by a departing traveller are exempt.
Dangerous drugs need a Department of Health export licence and a valid import certificate from the destination.
Opium and any drug covered by the Dangerous Drugs Ordinance may not be sent by post.
Proprietary Chinese medicines and 36 listed Chinese herbal medicines need a Department of Health export licence.
Rough diamonds can only be exported by TID-registered traders with a Kimberley Process export certificate for each consignment.

rules.statute: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615)
rules.article: Dealers in precious metals and stones registration
rules.rule: Businesses dealing in precious metals or stones with transactions of HK$120,000 or more must register with Customs.

rules.statute: Cross-boundary Movement of Physical Currency and Bearer Negotiable Instruments Ordinance (Cap. 629)
rules.rule: Exporting currency or bearer instruments worth over HK$120,000 as cargo in one batch needs an advance electronic declaration; CBNIs inside postal packets are outside this cargo rule.
Relics discovered in Hong Kong after the Ordinance took effect belong to the Government; the Ordinance has no general export licence for antiques.
Arms include air guns over 2 joules, stun guns, pepper sprays and crossbows over 6 kg; they need Police licences, and Munitions List items need a TID export licence.
Possessing prohibited weapons such as knuckledusters, gravity knives, throwing darts and spring-loaded batons is an offence.
Exporting goods bearing a forged trade mark or a false trade description is an offence; goods in transit are excluded.

rules.statute: 郵包物品進出口通關辦法
rules.statute_en: Regulations Governing Customs Clearance of Postal Parcels (TW)
rules.rule: Export parcels must not be banned exports and weigh at most 30 kg; FOB over USD 5,000 or goods under export rules need a formal export declaration; others declare name, quantity and value.

rules.statute: 臺灣地區與大陸地區人民關係條例
rules.statute_en: Act Governing Relations between the People of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area
rules.rule: Goods sent to the mainland are treated as exports and follow ordinary export inspection, quarantine and customs rules.

rules.statute: 臺灣地區與大陸地區貿易許可辦法
rules.statute_en: Regulations Governing Trade between the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area
rules.rule: Trade with the mainland must follow the permit rules; export documents must name the destination as mainland China.

rules.statute_en: Foreign Trade Act (TW)
rules.rule: Strategic high-tech commodities may not be exported without a licence, and end use and end user must be declared truthfully.

rules.statute: 戰略性高科技貨品輸出入管理辦法
rules.statute_en: Regulations Governing Export and Import of Strategic High-Tech Commodities (TW)
rules.rule: Exporters of strategic high-tech goods must first obtain an export licence with end-use documents.

rules.statute_en: Statute for Prevention and Control of Infectious Animal Diseases (TW)
rules.rule: Quarantinable items need export quarantine and a certificate when listed or when the importing country demands one.

rules.statute_en: Wildlife Conservation Act (TW)
rules.rule: Live wild animals and protected-species products need central authority consent to export.

rules.statute_en: Plant Protection and Quarantine Act (TW)
rules.rule: Where the importing country requires a phytosanitary certificate, the exporter applies for inspection and a certificate.

rules.statute_en: Statute for Prevention and Control of Infectious Animal Diseases (TW)
rules.rule: Animal products such as meat or animal-based pet food need an export quarantine certificate when the destination requires it.

rules.statute: 郵包物品進出口通關辦法
rules.statute_en: Regulations Governing Customs Clearance of Postal Parcels (TW)
rules.rule: No export restriction found for tea or dried goods; declare name, quantity and value.

rules.statute: 郵包物品進出口通關辦法
rules.statute_en: Regulations Governing Customs Clearance of Postal Parcels (TW)
rules.rule: No cosmetics export restriction found; normal declaration applies.

rules.statute: 郵包物品進出口通關辦法
rules.statute_en: Regulations Governing Customs Clearance of Postal Parcels (TW)
rules.rule: No Taiwan export-side statute specific to lithium batteries was found; carrier dangerous-goods conditions are not stated on the official pagehere.

rules.statute: 郵包物品進出口通關辦法
rules.statute_en: Regulations Governing Customs Clearance of Postal Parcels (TW)
rules.rule: No export restriction found for consumer radio devices, unless the item is a listed strategic high-tech commodity.

rules.statute: 郵包物品進出口通關辦法
rules.statute_en: Regulations Governing Customs Clearance of Postal Parcels (TW)
rules.rule: No alcohol export restriction found for parcels.

rules.statute: 郵包物品進出口通關辦法
rules.statute_en: Regulations Governing Customs Clearance of Postal Parcels (TW)
rules.rule: No tobacco export restriction found for parcels.

rules.statute_en: Tobacco Hazards Prevention Act (TW)
rules.rule: No one may make, import, sell, supply or display imitation tobacco products (e-cigarettes) or their parts, so a Taiwan seller cannot lawfully supply them.

rules.statute_en: Controlled Drugs Act (TW)
rules.rule: Schedule 1-2 controlled drugs may be imported or exported only by the TFDA factory; other schedules only by licensed firms.

rules.statute_en: Narcotics Hazard Prevention Act (TW)
rules.rule: Manufacturing, transporting or selling narcotic drugs is a serious crime.

rules.statute: 郵包物品進出口通關辦法
rules.statute_en: Regulations Governing Customs Clearance of Postal Parcels (TW)
rules.rule: No export restriction found for ordinary personal medicines.

rules.statute: 郵包物品進出口通關辦法
rules.statute_en: Regulations Governing Customs Clearance of Postal Parcels (TW)
rules.rule: No export restriction found for personal medical devices.

rules.statute: 洗錢防制物品出入境申報及通報辦法
rules.statute_en: Regulations on Declaring and Reporting Goods Crossing the Border under the Money Laundering Control Act (TW)
rules.rule: Gold worth over USD 20,000 sent by post on the same mailing day must be declared to customs.

rules.statute_en: Wildlife Conservation Act (TW)
rules.rule: Products of protected wildlife (e.g. some corals, ivory) need central authority consent to export.

rules.statute: 郵包物品進出口通關辦法
rules.statute_en: Regulations Governing Customs Clearance of Postal Parcels (TW)
rules.rule: Ordinary jewellery: normal export declaration.

rules.statute: 槍砲彈藥刀械管制條例
rules.statute_en: Controlling Guns, Ammunition and Knives Act (TW)
rules.rule: Guns, ammunition and their main parts may not be made, sold, transported or held without central authority permission.

rules.statute_en: Trademark Act
rules.rule: Selling, holding for sale, exporting or importing counterfeit-trademark goods is a crime, including online; customs detain suspect exports.

rules.statute_en: Cultural Heritage Preservation Act (TW)
rules.rule: National treasures and important antiquities may not be taken abroad without Executive Yuan approval; violation is a crime.

rules.statute_en: Cultural Heritage Preservation Act (TW)
rules.rule: Other century-old cultural objects need prior application only when temporarily taken out for exhibition, research or repair and returned.

rules.statute_en: Money Laundering Control Act (TW)
rules.rule: Cash, securities, gold and other high-value items above set thresholds must be declared, including when sent by courier or post.

rules.statute: 洗錢防制物品出入境申報及通報辦法
rules.statute_en: Regulations on Declaring and Reporting Goods Crossing the Border under the Money Laundering Control Act (TW)
rules.rule: Declaration thresholds: foreign/HK/Macao cash over USD 10,000, NT$ cash over NT$100,000, securities over USD 10,000, gold over USD 20,000; post counted per sender per mailing day.

rules.statute: 臺灣地區與大陸地區人民關係條例
rules.statute_en: Act Governing Relations between the People of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area
rules.rule: Mainland-issued currency may not enter or leave Taiwan above the FSC limit; the numeric limit was not stated on the official pagein the fetched text.

rules.statute_en: Regulations Governing the Handling of Postal Items (TW)
rules.rule: Flammable, explosive or other dangerous goods may not be posted. Chunghwa Post's international parcel terms name 3C products containing lithium batteries as prohibited dangerous items.

rules.statute_en: Regulations Governing the Handling of Postal Items (TW)
rules.rule: Chunghwa Post's cross-strait mailing guide lists phones, lithium batteries, power banks, tablets, laptops and items with built-in lithium batteries as not mailable to the mainland.

rules.statute: 危險物品空運管理辦法
rules.statute_en: Regulations for the Air Transport of Dangerous Goods (TW)
rules.rule: Dangerous goods may not be sent or hidden in air mail unless tendered under the technical instructions and the mail rules; violations are fined NT$20,000-100,000 under the Civil Aviation Act (per Chunghwa Post).

rules.statute_en: Postal Act (TW)
rules.rule: Legal basis: the mail rules, including categories of prohibited items and their disposal, are set by the competent authority and approved by the Executive Yuan.

rules.statute_en: Regulations Governing the Handling of Postal Items (TW)
rules.rule: Live animals may not be posted, except bees, silkworms, leeches, parasites exchanged between registered institutions, pest-control insects and (to Japan) earthworms.

rules.statute_en: Regulations Governing the Handling of Postal Items (TW)
rules.rule: Opium, morphine and other narcotics may not be posted, except with a transport permit or as court evidence, or to abroad for medical/scientific use where allowed.

rules.statute: 大陸地區發行之幣券進出入臺灣地區限額規定（依臺灣地區與大陸地區人民關係條例第38條訂定）
rules.statute_en: Limits on Mainland-Issued Currency Entering or Leaving Taiwan (under Cross-Strait Act Art. 38)
rules.agency: Financial Supervisory Commission (Banking Bureau law database)
rules.rule: Mainland-issued currency (RMB) moving in or out of Taiwan is capped at RMB 20,000. It covers post and courier via 洗錢防制物品出入境申報及通報辦法 第3條第3項; sealing the excess at customs applies to travellers only.

rules.statute: 中央銀行公告（新臺幣現鈔進出境；經財政部關務署出入境常見問題轉述）
rules.statute_en: Central Bank (Taiwan) notice on NT$ banknotes crossing the border (as stated in Customs FAQ)
rules.rule: NT$ banknotes may not be sent across the border by cargo, courier or post without special Central Bank approval. Customs cites the Central Bank notice but no article number.

rules.statute: 空運快遞貨物通關辦法
rules.statute_en: Regulations Governing Customs Clearance of Air Express Consignments (TW)
rules.rule: Air express consignments must weigh 70 kg or less per piece and must not be banned, controlled, IP-infringing, fresh farm produce, live plants/animals or protected wildlife; otherwise they cannot clear in the express zone.

rules.statute: 中华人民共和国海关法
rules.statute_en: Customs Law of the PRC
rules.agency: NPC Standing Committee (text via MFA PDF)
rules.rule: Personal items sent out by post must be for own use and in reasonable quantity, and are subject to customs control.

rules.statute: 海关总署公告2010年第43号（经海关总署公告2024年第176号修改）
rules.statute_en: GACC Announcement No. 43 (2010), as amended by No. 176 (2024)
rules.article: 第二点（2024年第176号第一项修改）
rules.agency: General Administration of Customs (via MOFCOM gazette; customs.gov.cn returned HTTP 412)
rules.rule: Personal parcels sent from the mainland to Hong Kong, Macao or Taiwan are capped at RMB 800 per parcel (RMB 1,000 to other places).

rules.statute: 中华人民共和国出口管制法
rules.statute_en: Export Control Law of the PRC
rules.rule: Listed dual-use, military and other controlled items (incl. related technical data) need an export licence; unlisted consumer goods are affected only if risk-flagged.

rules.statute: 中华人民共和国禁止进出境物品表 / 中华人民共和国限制进出境物品表（海关总署令第43号）
rules.statute_en: PRC Lists of Goods Prohibited / Restricted from Entry and Exit (Customs Order No. 43)
rules.article: 禁止出境物品 第4项
rules.rule: Endangered and precious animals (including specimens) may not leave China.

rules.statute: 中华人民共和国进出境动植物检疫法
rules.statute_en: Law of the PRC on Entry and Exit Animal and Plant Quarantine
rules.rule: Animals and animal/plant products must be declared for quarantine before export; animals needing isolation are quarantined at designated sites.

rules.statute: 中华人民共和国禁止进出境物品表 / 中华人民共和国限制进出境物品表（海关总署令第43号）
rules.statute_en: PRC Lists of Goods Prohibited / Restricted from Entry and Exit (Customs Order No. 43)
rules.article: 禁止出境物品 第4项
rules.rule: Endangered and precious plants, their seeds and propagation material may not leave China.

rules.statute: 中华人民共和国进出境动植物检疫法
rules.statute_en: Law of the PRC on Entry and Exit Animal and Plant Quarantine
rules.rule: Plants and plant products must be declared for export quarantine before leaving.

rules.statute: 中华人民共和国进出境动植物检疫法
rules.statute_en: Law of the PRC on Entry and Exit Animal and Plant Quarantine
rules.rule: Animal and plant products (e.g. meat products, animal-based pet food) must be declared for export quarantine.

rules.statute: 中华人民共和国海关法
rules.statute_en: Customs Law of the PRC
rules.agency: NPC Standing Committee (text via MFA PDF)
rules.rule: No mainland export ban found for tea or ordinary dried goods sent as personal items; own-use and reasonable-quantity rule applies.

rules.statute: 中华人民共和国海关法
rules.statute_en: Customs Law of the PRC
rules.agency: NPC Standing Committee (text via MFA PDF)
rules.rule: No cosmetics-specific export restriction found; own-use and reasonable-quantity rule applies.

rules.statute: 禁止寄递物品管理规定（附禁止寄递物品指导目录）
rules.statute_en: Provisions on Items Prohibited from Postal Delivery, with Guiding Catalogue (PRC)
rules.article: 第3条、第5条；目录 第六类、第十一类
rules.rule: Posting dangerous goods is banned; the catalog lists metallic lithium and wet accumulators. Consumer lithium-ion batteries are not named; their postal limit is not stated on the official page.

rules.statute: 中华人民共和国禁止进出境物品表 / 中华人民共和国限制进出境物品表（海关总署令第43号）
rules.statute_en: PRC Lists of Goods Prohibited / Restricted from Entry and Exit (Customs Order No. 43)
rules.article: 限制出境物品 第4项
rules.rule: Radio transceivers and communications encryption equipment are restricted exports.

rules.statute: 中华人民共和国海关法
rules.statute_en: Customs Law of the PRC
rules.agency: NPC Standing Committee (text via MFA PDF)
rules.rule: No alcohol export restriction found for personal parcels; own-use and reasonable-quantity rule applies.

rules.statute: 中华人民共和国烟草专卖法实施条例
rules.statute_en: Implementing Regulations of the Tobacco Monopoly Law of the PRC
rules.rule: Mailing tobacco products beyond the quantity set by State Council departments is penalised; the numeric mail limit was not stated on the official page.

rules.statute: 国家烟草专卖局 国家邮政局关于电子烟产品、雾化物、电子烟用烟碱等限量寄递的通告
rules.statute_en: State Tobacco Monopoly Administration / State Post Bureau notice on postal limits for e-cigarette products
rules.article: 第一点至第三点、第五点
rules.agency: State Tobacco Monopoly Administration / State Post Bureau
rules.rule: E-cigarette mailing is quantity-limited, and the same limits apply to cross-border mailing; one parcel per person per day.

rules.statute: 中华人民共和国禁止进出境物品表 / 中华人民共和国限制进出境物品表（海关总署令第43号）
rules.statute_en: PRC Lists of Goods Prohibited / Restricted from Entry and Exit (Customs Order No. 43)
rules.article: 禁止出境物品 第1项（援引禁止进境物品 第4、5项）
rules.rule: Narcotics, psychotropic drugs and highly toxic poisons may not leave China.

rules.statute_en: PRC Lists of Goods Prohibited / Restricted from Entry and Exit (Customs Order No. 43)
rules.article: 限制出境物品 第5项
rules.rule: Precious Chinese medicinal materials are restricted exports.

rules.statute: 中华人民共和国海关法
rules.statute_en: Customs Law of the PRC
rules.agency: NPC Standing Committee (text via MFA PDF)
rules.rule: Ordinary personal medicines: own-use and reasonable-quantity rule; no further export restriction found.

rules.statute: 中华人民共和国海关法
rules.statute_en: Customs Law of the PRC
rules.agency: NPC Standing Committee (text via MFA PDF)
rules.rule: No medical-device export restriction found for personal parcels.

rules.statute: 中华人民共和国禁止进出境物品表 / 中华人民共和国限制进出境物品表（海关总署令第43号）
rules.statute_en: PRC Lists of Goods Prohibited / Restricted from Entry and Exit (Customs Order No. 43)
rules.article: 限制出境物品 第1项
rules.rule: Gold, silver and other precious metals and articles made of them are restricted exports.

rules.statute: 中华人民共和国禁止进出境物品表 / 中华人民共和国限制进出境物品表（海关总署令第43号）
rules.statute_en: PRC Lists of Goods Prohibited / Restricted from Entry and Exit (Customs Order No. 43)
rules.article: 禁止出境物品 第1项（援引禁止进境物品 第1项）
rules.rule: All weapons, imitation weapons, ammunition and explosives may not leave China.

rules.statute: 中华人民共和国知识产权海关保护条例
rules.statute_en: Regulations on Customs Protection of Intellectual Property Rights (PRC)
rules.rule: Import and export of goods infringing intellectual property rights is prohibited.

rules.statute: 中华人民共和国文物保护法
rules.statute_en: Cultural Relics Protection Law of the PRC
rules.rule: State-owned relics, precious privately-owned relics and other relics on the banned list may not leave China, except approved exhibitions.

rules.statute: 中华人民共和国文物保护法
rules.statute_en: Cultural Relics Protection Law of the PRC
rules.rule: Any relic sent abroad must pass a designated review body and get an export permit; posting relics requires a customs declaration.

rules.statute: 中华人民共和国禁止进出境物品表 / 中华人民共和国限制进出境物品表（海关总署令第43号）
rules.statute_en: PRC Lists of Goods Prohibited / Restricted from Entry and Exit (Customs Order No. 43)
rules.article: 限制出境物品 第2、3项
rules.rule: Chinese currency, foreign currency and securities are restricted exports.

rules.statute: 中国人民银行公告〔2004〕第18号
rules.statute_en: People's Bank of China Announcement No. 18 (2004)
rules.rule: Each traveller may carry at most RMB 20,000 in or out per trip; no postal-specific cash limit was found.

rules.statute: 携带外币现钞出入境管理暂行办法（汇发〔2003〕102号）
rules.statute_en: Interim Measures on Carrying Foreign Currency Cash In and Out of the PRC (SAFE 2003 No. 102)
rules.rule: Travellers may take out up to USD 5,000 equivalent in foreign cash without a permit; more needs a bank or SAFE permit (traveller rule).

rules.statute: 中华人民共和国药品管理法
rules.statute_en: Drug Administration Law of the PRC
rules.agency: NPC Standing Committee (text via MOFCOM 全球法规网, which cites 全国人大网; npc.gov.cn and flk.npc.gov.cn served no law text)
rules.rule: Exporting narcotic drugs or listed psychotropic drugs requires an export permit from the national drug regulator.

rules.statute: 锂电池邮件航空运输管理办法（民航局 国家邮政局，2014）
rules.statute_en: Measures on Air Transport of Lithium Batteries in Mail (CAAC / State Post Bureau, 2014)
rules.agency: CAAC / State Post Bureau (CAAC news release)
rules.rule: Air mail may carry lithium batteries only installed in equipment (cell <=20 Wh, battery <=100 Wh; lithium metal <=1 g/cell, 2 g/battery) under an approved postal procedure; in 2014 China Post had none, so air-mailing lithium batteries was not allowed. Current status not stated on the official page.

rules.statute: 船舶载运危险货物安全监督管理规定（交通运输部令2024年第14号）
rules.statute_en: Provisions on Safety Supervision of Dangerous Goods Carried by Ships (MOT Order No. 14, 2024, PRC)
rules.agency: Ministry of Transport (via gov.cn; same text on xxgk.mot.gov.cn)
rules.rule: Sea dangerous-goods channel only: packaged dangerous goods on ships must meet the IMDG Code; goods in the IMDG Part 3 list (where lithium batteries appear as Class 9) are in scope. UN3480/3481/3090/3091 are not named here; they are in the incorporated IMDG list (not stated on the official pageon official pages).

rules.statute: 船舶载运危险货物安全监督管理规定（交通运输部令2024年第14号）
rules.statute_en: Provisions on Safety Supervision of Dangerous Goods Carried by Ships (MOT Order No. 14, 2024, PRC)
rules.agency: Ministry of Transport (via gov.cn; same text on xxgk.mot.gov.cn)
rules.rule: Sea dangerous-goods channel only: before handover the shipper gives the carrier a safe-transport declaration and safety data sheet (proper name, class, quantity, hazards) and reports to MSA; hiding dangerous goods in ordinary cargo is banned.

rules.statute: 船舶载运危险货物安全监督管理规定（交通运输部令2024年第14号）
rules.statute_en: Provisions on Safety Supervision of Dangerous Goods Carried by Ships (MOT Order No. 14, 2024, PRC)
rules.agency: Ministry of Transport (via gov.cn; same text on xxgk.mot.gov.cn)
rules.rule: Sea dangerous-goods channel only: the ship's dangerous-goods declaration must be filed with MSA 24 hours before entering or leaving port and approved before sailing.
